Description


The Roadside Ecology Center (REC) at Southern Illinois University Carbondale (SIU) invites applications for eight (8) full-time Interdisciplinary Scientists. These positions conduct field-based ecological research and environmental compliance work in support of the Center’s mission to assess and mitigate the impacts of transportation infrastructure on wildlife and ecosystems. The REC operates through a long-term partnership between SIU and the Illinois Department of Transportation (IDOT), serving the environmental compliance needs of the southern third of Illinois while advancing applied research in road ecology.

Positions are assigned to either the Biological Team—focused on wildlife, threatened and endangered species, and multi-taxa surveys—or the Wetland Team, focused on wetland delineation, functional assessment, and aquatic resources. All positions require multi-taxa competency, strong field skills, GIS proficiency, and collaborative work across disciplines.

IDOT and the REC seek scientists who are research-minded, multi-taxa generalists. The research emphasis is on identifying resource concerns, determining appropriate mitigation and offset strategies, evaluating current best management practices, and conducting defensible research on avoidance and minimization in the built environment. 

Salary is competitive and commensurate with qualifications and experience, while also considering internal equity.



Examples of Duties

Conduct field surveys for threatened and endangered species across multiple taxa (plants, herpetofauna, birds, mammals, invertebrates, fish), including presence/absence surveys, habitat assessments, and population monitoring; obtain necessary state and federal handling permits. 
Complete environmental compliance documentation—biological assessments, impact evaluations, and mitigation plans—for IDOT transportation projects, and prepare technical reports for submission to IDOT and regulatory agencies. 
Biological Team: Execute wildlife surveys using standardized protocols, conduct road mortality assessments, and evaluate the potential for and effectiveness of mitigation strategies for wildlife populations and ecosystem function. Wetland Team: Perform wetland delineations following U.S. Army Corps of Engineers methodology, conduct rapid functional assessments, complete jurisdictional determinations, and assess mitigation site performance. 
Collect, manage, and quality-check field data using mobile devices, GPS units, and standardized datasheets; respond to time-sensitive field requests and adapt to changing priorities during construction seasons. 
Develop and implement applied research projects addressing knowledge gaps in road ecology, with emphasis on avoidance, minimization, and mitigation effectiveness; contribute findings to peer-reviewed publications, technical reports, and conference presentations. 
Create, maintain, and analyze spatial datasets using ArcGIS or QGIS; produce maps and spatial summaries for reports and publications; contribute to Center-wide data management systems. 
Collaborate across biological and wetland teams; maintain professional relationships with IDOT personnel and regulatory agency staff; mentor undergraduate and graduate students involved in REC research.

Qualifications


Minimum Qualifications:


Required for All Positions: 

Master’s degree in ecology, wildlife biology, botany, environmental science, natural resource management, or a closely related field.
Minimum of three years of professional experience conducting ecological field surveys (academic research, consulting, or agency work acceptable). 
Demonstrated record of peer-reviewed publication in applied ecology or conservation biology, commensurate with the university-level Assistant Scientist classification 
Demonstrated competency in species identification across at least two major taxonomic groups. 
Proficiency with GIS software (ArcGIS, QGIS), including spatial data creation, analysis, and map production. 
Driver’s license with clean driving record; physical ability to conduct field work in variable terrain and conditions, including carrying equipment up to 40 lbs.

Additional Requirements – Biological Team: 

Experience conducting wildlife surveys using standardized protocols (e.g., point counts, acoustic monitoring, camera trapping, mist netting) and familiarity with threatened and endangered species of Illinois or the Midwest.

Additional Requirements – Wetland Team: 

Demonstrated experience conducting wetland delineations following U.S. Army Corps of Engineers methodology; proficiency in Midwest herbaceous wetland plant identification; familiarity with Section 404 permitting and wetland mitigation requirements.

Preferred (All Positions):

PhD in a relevant discipline is strongly preferred, or five or more years of professional experience in road ecology, transportation agency work, or environmental consulting. 
 Familiarity with NEPA, ESA (Sections 7 and 10), or Clean Water Act compliance processes; professional certifications (e.g., CWB, PWS). 
Proficiency with statistical software (R, Python); experience with remote sensing, spatial modeling, or advanced GIS; track record of peer-reviewed publications or technical reports. 
Familiarity with Illinois flora, fauna, natural communities, and ecoregions, particularly southern Illinois.
Required documents: Please submit a letter of application, CV/Resume, and three references.

Description
The Department of Environment and Society (ENVS) at Utah State University (USU) invites applications for a tenure-track position of Assistant Professor with expertise in environmental and natural resources policy. We seek applicants who work at the science-policy interface, connecting scientific knowledge with policy development, design, implementation, or adoption, to support environmental and natural resource management, stewardship, and decision making. Possible areas of policy expertise could include air quality, climate, critical minerals, energy, land use, public lands, outdoor recreation, water, or wildlife, as examples. We welcome applications from those working across an array of environmental and natural resource contexts, with relevance to the state of Utah especially welcome. Teaching expectations will include a combination of online/virtual and in-person courses that contribute to the Department’s curriculum. This tenure-track, full-time academic year (nine-month) position is based at the USU main campus in Logan. The emphasis for the position is 50% research, 40% teaching/advising, and 10% service. The position will start August 2027. Background information is available on the webpages for the Department of Environment and Society and its home, the S.J. and Jessie E. Quinney College of Agriculture and Natural Resources.

Application review will begin December 1, 2026. The position will remain open until filled, but application by the date above is encouraged for full consideration. Candidates from all backgrounds and populations are encouraged to apply. For further information contact the search committee chair, Dr. Cat Edgeley ([email removed]).

Responsibilities
The successful candidate will lead a research program that investigates environmental and natural resources policy.
Teaching includes courses that contribute to the Department’s curriculum areas in environmental studies, environmental science and sustainability, geography, and recreation resource management. The successful candidate could expect to teach courses in the area of environmental and natural resources policy but might also be asked to contribute in other departmental curricular areas.
Courses may be taught at both undergraduate and graduate levels and may be delivered in person, via virtual or online learning, or in a blended format. 
Student advising includes mentoring undergraduate researchers and advising graduate students in a supportive learning environment that promotes the success of all students.
Community engagement, broadly defined, is encouraged. Community engagement in research, teaching, and/or service activities is valued by the Department and is integrated into our mission, climate, and culture. 
Service includes participation in faculty duties on campus as well as professional involvement off campus. 

Minimum Qualifications
An earned PhD (or JD with academic experience) at date-of-hire in a field related to environmental or natural resources policy or science.

Preferred Qualifications
Demonstrated application of research to environmental and natural resource policy.
Familiarity with policy-related research methods, accompanied by the instructional capacity and willingness to teach coursework in this area. 
A publication record consistent with career stage.
Demonstrated potential to build and maintain a productive research program, including the ability to secure competitive external funding.
Evidence of successful collaboration with natural and social scientists as well as practitioners across disciplines.
Demonstrated interest in community-engaged research or outreach that complements USU’s Land Grant mission. 
Prior teaching and mentoring experience.
Experience with or the desire to learn about virtual and online course delivery. 
Demonstrated ability to contribute to a learning community of members from a range of backgrounds and experiences and to foster a sense of belonging for all students.

To Apply: Applicants must submit all application materials electronically via the Utah State University Human Resources website, https://careers-usu.icims.com/jobs/10827/assistant-professor---environmental-and-natural-resources-policy/job.  Along with completing the online application, applicants will upload or insert the following:
Cover letter (2-page maximum)
CV
Research statement that covers research experience and interests (2-page maximum)
Teaching statement that covers teaching experience and philosophy, including in fostering the success of students from all backgrounds (2-page maximum)
Contact information for three references

College/Department Highlights
The Department of Environment and Society applies social, environmental, and interdisciplinary sciences to understand human-environment interactions at a range of scales. Our faculty address complex environmental and societal challenges through innovative research and extension, generating practical insights for managers, policymakers, and practitioners. We provide graduate and undergraduate education in environmental, social and interdisciplinary sciences, recreation resource management, and geography. Together, we value holistic practices and community engagement for a more sustainable tomorrow. 

The S.J. & Jessie E. Quinney College of Agriculture & Natural Resources (QANR) at USU is known for its research, traditions, and community engagement, with recent highlights including new leadership, special events, and innovative projects. QANR offers 12 departments covering agriculture, food, environment, technology, design, and more, plus associate degrees and technical certificates at statewide campuses.

University Highlights
As Utah’s student-centered, land-grant research university, Utah State University expands opportunity and strengthens communities across the state through learning, discovery, extension, and engagement. Founded in 1888, USU now holds two Carnegie distinctions: R1 status for very high research activity and the Carnegie Community Engagement Classification. Its innovative research and scholarship is grounded in reciprocal partnerships with local, regional, and global communities, advancing knowledge and serving the public good across Utah, the nation, and the world. With over 50 world-class research facilities and the nation’s second-oldest undergraduate research program, USU prepares students to become active, civically engaged leaders who can address critical societal challenges.

USU enrolls over 29,800 students, both online and in person at locations throughout the state. Utah State’s 30 locations include a main campus in Logan, Utah, residential campuses in Price and Blanding, and six additional statewide campuses, along with education centers serving every county. USU educates students from all 50 states and more than 80 countries. For over 100 years, USU Extension has served and engaged Utahns, serving every county in the state.

Competing at the NCAA Division I level in 16 sports, USU is a proud member of the Pac-12 Conference, which it joined July 1, 2026. The Aggies capped a historic final season in the Mountain West by capturing nine combined regular-season and tournament titles in 2025-26, with five teams advancing to postseason play. This tradition of excellence extends to the classroom, where 232 student-athletes earned academic honors, and to the community, where USU ranked second nationally in Division I service hours, with nine teams placing in the top 10 for community service.

Utah State is dedicated to fostering a community where all individuals feel respected, valued, and supported and where diversity of thought and culture are cultivated. We seek to recruit, hire, and retain people from all walks of life who will champion excellence in education, research, discovery, outreach, and service. We believe that promoting a strong sense of community and belonging empowers and engages all members of USU to thrive and be successful. Forbes recognized our commitment to employees when it named Utah State the best employer in Utah in 2023. Learn more about USU.

Description
Pacific States Marine Fisheries Commission is recruiting motivated and detail-oriented candidates to assist the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) as a Fishery Biologist 2 - Data Analyst at the Western Fisheries Research Center (WFRC), Columbia River Research Laboratory. We are seeking a quantitatively skilled individual to provide data management, coding, and analytical support to WFRC's Quantitative Ecology Team across a diverse array of fisheries research and monitoring projects.
 
This is a full-time, benefits-eligible position with an anticipated start date of November 16th, 2026.

Major Duties & Responsibilities
· Data Preparation & Management: Clean, structure, quality-check, and manage large fisheries monitoring datasets including acoustic/radio/passive-integrated-transponder telemetry and environmental variables. Maintain metadata documentation and prepare for data for public release.
· Coding & Reproducible Workflows: Execute, maintain, and document code (e.g., R scripts and reproducible reporting tools) for routine and complex statistical and modeling analyses under the guidance of senior quantitative ecologists.
· Analytical Support: Assist senior scientists with running statistical analyses and simulation models, including prepping data inputs for mark-recapture models integrated population models (IPMs), fitting models using standard or customized computer code, formatting output, and assisting with running mechanistic simulation models.
· Documentation & Technical Writing: Assist in writing and compiling technical reports, maintaining thorough documentation of code/data pipelines, and contributing draft sections, tables, and figures for co-authored peer-reviewed publications.
· Communication & Collaboration: Create clear data visualizations, summary tables, and presentation slides to help communicate model outputs and analytical findings to team members, collaborators, and stakeholders.

Qualifications & Knowledge Required
· Education: Bachelor's degree with 2+ years of specialized experience, or a Master's degree in Fisheries Science, Quantitative Ecology, Biometrics, Statistics, Data Science, or a closely related natural resources field.
· Quantitative & Coding Skills: Strong proficiency in programming languages (such as R) for data wrangling, statistical analysis, and graphics generation. Experience working with complex ecological or telemetry datasets is highly desirable.
· Methodological Familiarity: Basic understanding or prior exposure to mark-recapture estimation, Bayesian/frequentist statistical concepts, or population modeling fundamentals.
· Technical Writing & Organization: Strong technical writing ability, excellent attention to detail, and a commitment to reproducible data analysis and code documentation.
· Communication: Good interpersonal and communication skills to collaborate effectively within a multi-disciplinary research team.

Essential Functions:   
At the lower end of the range, Fishery Biologists have a solid working knowledge of established scientific methods and techniques to perform recurring assignments of moderate difficulty.  Methods and techniques are well established, apply to most situations, and do not require significant deviations.  Resource planning reports generated by employees at this level involve conventional biological concerns.  Reports generated may be short-range management plans or portions of annual work plans.  Lower range work examples include:
Following existing protocols for fish health screenings, conduct tissue sample collection, bacterial testing and analyses, blood collection and analyses, parasite identification, and necropsies on experimental fish populations.
Recommend modifications of existing research protocols.
Design data collection forms and set up research databases for integration of data.
Compile and analyze data for reports, prepare graphics, contribute to or write papers for peer-reviewed journals, and present research results at professional meetings.
Plan, schedule, and conduct behavioral, physiological, morphological, and survival evaluations of hatchery and/or experimental fish populations.
Oversee and assist with fish culture tasks for study purposes and recommend procedure variations. Write or contribute to papers and reports for publication, and compile reports on results of data collection and analysis.
Prepare and deliver formal and informal presentations at seminars, meetings, etc.
Work with state, federal and regional fishery management councils to provide data on fisheries catch and effort and population trends as well as biology of marine fish species.
Conduct limited physical and biological watershed, stream, and fish habitat assessments. Responsible for conducting data investigation and research, drafting technical report, database management, GIS for all physical and biological data, and survey and inventory results.
At the upper end of the range, the Fishery Biologist has specialized knowledge and demonstrated competence in advanced techniques of a complex area of fish biology sufficient to serve as a troubleshooter or specialist.  The employee is competent to modify or adapt standard techniques, processes and procedures, and to assess, select, apply precedents and devise strategies and plans to overcome significant problems related to species production, protection, habitat restoration, or program management and evaluation. Planning reports generated by employees at this level assess the impact of various multi-faceted management or public practices on a resource. Upper range work examples include:

Use biological information to evaluate run profiles and habitat suitability in stocked streams within a major geographical area.
Develop comprehensive management plans to insure preservation, protection, and enhancement of habitats.
Plan, design and implement research studies on fish health and/or nutrition.
Analyze and report biological and/or genetic information affecting future selection, rearing, and spawning activities.
Prepare both quarterly progress and annual reports on run status and hatchery or fish facility operations.
Monitor and evaluate hatching, rearing and planting of fish.
Evaluate and monitor adult return rates.
Develop new rearing strategies.
Prepare fish habitat measurement plans or management plans for a watershed or large geographic area.
Diagnose various fish diseases or nutritional disorders in experimental populations or brood stock. Develop modifications to existing health protocols as well as experimental protocols.
Write publishable reports of research and project findings.
Knowledge Required by the Position: 

Knowledge of the scientific method.
Knowledge of Windows-based computer applications such as word processing, spreadsheets, e-mail, publishing software, presentation software, database software, topographic software, bibliographic software, and statistical analysis packages.
Knowledge of technical writing protocols.
Knowledge of advanced statistical analysis and mathematics.
Additional Mandatory Skills:  

valid driver's license
specific software (spreadsheet, word processing, database management, GIS, statistical analysis, behavioral analysis, bibliographic)
oral communication skills                              
written communication skills              
 

Physical Demands:
Demands generally range from sedentary to moderate --where there is walking, climbing stairs and ladders, reaching, lifting, bending, or extended periods of standing. Some Fishery Biologists in this range have rigorous physical demands where they must be able to handle buckets of water or gear weighing from 40 - 50 pounds, engage in long daily periods of hiking, camp out for extended periods, or maintain footing in fast-moving water.

Work Environment:
Some work is performed in an office setting with adequate lighting, heating and ventilation. Some work may be performed in a laboratory setting which exposes the biologist to odors, chemicals, fish blood, and molds. The employee must use safety precautions including MSDS, gloves, hood, and eye protection. Some employees may work on narrow, elevated walkways and platforms that are over or adjacent to water. Field work involves exposure to all types of weather, slippery rocks or docks, trails, irregular terrain, insects, poison oak, rough or fast-moving water, or cold water temperatures. Work at high elevations or aboard boats may be required.


Qualifications
Minimum Qualification Requirements:
A range of education and experience may be presented.  At the lower end of the range, candidates must present successful completion of a full 4-year course of study in an accredited college or university leading to a bachelor's or higher degree that included a major in biological science with at least 6 semester hours in aquatic subjects and at least 12 semester hours in the animal sciences.  In addition to the undergraduate degree requirement, candidates for positions at the lower end of the range must also present 1 year of Specialized Experience** OR 2 years of progressively higher graduate education leading to a master's degree in fields directly related to the position being filled. An equivalent combination of experience and education is also qualifying.
At the upper end of the range, in addition to the undergraduate course of study described above, candidates must also must present one year of Specialized Experience**  OR  3 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a Ph. D. degree or equivalent doctoral degree in fields directly related to the position being filled.  An equivalent combination of experience and education is also qualifying.
**Specialized Experience is experience that equips the applicant with the knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform successfully the duties of the position and is typically in or related to the work of the position being filled.  To be creditable, specialized experience must have been equivalent to at least the next lower level in the normal line of progression for the position being filled.

Full-Year Employees working at least 30 hours a week are covered by the Company's Life, LTD and AD&D plan. An employee receives up to 120 hours of vacation during their first three years of service. After that, the amount of vacation increases every three years of service up to a maximum of 192 hours per year.

Overview:
The Department of Environment and Society (ENVS) at Utah State University (USU) invites applications for one to two postdoctoral fellow positions supporting existing programs in Geographic Information Science, Remote Sensing, and Geospatial Artificial Intelligence (GeoAI). The position(s) will have both teaching and research responsibilities, with teaching as the majority of the role. Fellows will have a designated faculty mentor.
 These full-time, twelve-month positions are based at the USU main campus in Logan, Utah. A remote start prior to relocating may be negotiable. Position length may be negotiable up to two years. Salary is competitive and commensurate with experience, with excellent benefits. Positions have a start date as early as January 1, 2027 and no later than August 16, 2027. Application review begins 16 November 2026. The application window will remain open, with applications reviewed on an ongoing basis, until positions are filled. For further information, contact search committee chair and department head Claudia Radel at [email removed].
 Responsibilities:  
Course Instruction: Teach up to 18 credits. Courses will focus on GIS, remote sensing, and geospatial AI at both undergraduate and graduate levels and may be delivered via online, in-person, or in a blended format, with greater weight towards online deliveries. Fellows will step into established courses and supervise a remote sensing and GeoAI capstone course focused on applied, project-based learning in natural resource and environmental applications. Course areas may include intro and advanced GeoAI, applied remote sensing, geospatial programming in Python and R, ethics related to geospatial data, Google Earth Engine, geovisualization techniques, and database management.
Curriculum Development: Update course material as needed to maintain relevancy of curriculum by keeping pace with industry advancements in GIS, remote sensing and geospatial AI.
Student Mentoring: Provide academic and research mentorship to a diverse set of students pursuing interests in geospatial fields. Foster a supportive and inclusive learning environment that promotes student success.
Research: Carry out research-related activities. Contribute to research projects as appropriate across diverse potential units at USU including the Department of Environment & Society, the Department of Wildland Resources, the Ecology Center, and the Utah Water Research Laboratory, among others. Fellows also will have the opportunity to complete, publish, or otherwise advance research from their doctoral work in preparation for future academic or professional positions.
 Minimum Qualifications:  
PhD advanced candidacy status by time-of-hire in geography or related quantitative field, with a focus on geospatial science in a human-environment or natural resources context.
Demonstrated expertise in GIS, remote sensing, and geospatial artificial intelligence.
 Preferred Qualifications: 
Prior teaching experience, with an emphasis on delivering innovative courses in geospatial science of human-environment interactions. 
Prior experience with online course delivery. 
A demonstrated ability to effectively collaborate in an interdisciplinary academic setting. 
 Non-US citizens are welcome to apply, and J-1 visa sponsorship may be possible. USU will not sponsor H-1B visas for this position. 
 To Apply: Applicants must submit all application materials electronically via the Utah State University Human Resources website (https://careers-usu.icims.com/jobs/10853/postdoctoral-fellow-ii---remote-sensing-%26-geoai-in-natural-resources-and-the-environment/job). Along with completing the online application, applicants will upload or insert the following:
Cover letter, including information on both teaching and research interests (2-page maximum)
Statement of teaching experience and philosophy (2-page maximum)
CV
Contact information for three references
 Department Highlights:
The Department of Environment and Society applies social, environmental, and interdisciplinary sciences to understand human-environment interactions at a range of scales. Our faculty address complex environmental and societal challenges through innovative research and extension, generating practical insights for managers, policymakers, and practitioners. We provide graduate and undergraduate education in environmental, social and interdisciplinary sciences, recreation resource management, and geography. Together, we value holistic practices and community engagement for a more sustainable tomorrow.

Description
POSITION OVERVIEW 

The College of Forestry, Wildlife and Environment (CFWE) at Auburn University invites applications for Coordinator of its shooting sports program. The Coordinator provides strategic and operational leadership for a comprehensive program encompassing instruction, curriculum development, personnel supervision, facility and equipment management, risk management, and partnership development across archery and multiple firearm disciplines (pistol, rifle, shotgun).

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

·         Strategic & Operational Leadership: Provide vision and long-term goals for curriculum, enrollment, staffing, range facilities, and program sustainability.

·         Curriculum & Instruction: Develop and oversee credit/noncredit courses, workshops, and events. Serve as an instructor or Range Safety Officer as needed.

·         Safety & Compliance: Establish and enforce standardized operating procedures, range rules, emergency response plans, and equipment safety standards in compliance with University policies and applicable laws.

·         Personnel Management: Recruit, train, schedule, supervise, and evaluate instructors, student employees, and volunteers.

·         Facility & Asset Management: Oversee operations, maintenance, and infrastructure for range facilities (including the off-campus Crooked Oaks facility). Manage inventory, procurement, storage, and maintenance of firearms, archery gear, and supplies.

·         Administration & Budget: Manage program budgets, fee-based revenues, recordkeeping, registration logistics, and outcome assessments. Prepare performance reports for leadership.

·         Partnerships & Outreach: Collaborate with University units, state/federal agencies, conservation organizations, donors, and the CFWE Development Office to support fundraising, grants, and student recruitment.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

·         Bachelor’s degree in wildlife sciences, natural resources, education, recreation, sport management, public administration, or a related field.

·         5+ years of progressively responsible experience in shooting sports instruction, range operations, or outdoor education administration.

·         Demonstrated hands-on experience safely instructing firearms and/or archery.

·         Proven supervisory and team management experience.

·         Strong working knowledge of range safety, risk management, equipment maintenance, and emergency protocols.

·         Demonstrated administrative ability in budgeting, recordkeeping, and standard office software.

·         Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.

·         Ability to obtain and maintain required University certifications.

 

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS

·         Master’s degree in a relevant field.

·         Nationally recognized instructor, coach, or range safety certifications in multiple disciplines (archery, pistol, rifle, shotgun, muzzleloading).

·         Current First Aid, CPR, AED, or trauma-response training.

·         Experience managing shooting ranges, outdoor facilities, or complex experiential learning programs.

·         Background in higher education curriculum development, adult-learning practices, hunter education, or collegiate shooting sports.

WORKING CONDITIONS & EXPECTATIONS Requires regular work at outdoor/off-campus range facilities, occasional evening/weekend hours, travel, and physical ability to handle and transport gear in outdoor conditions. Must meet Auburn University requirements regarding driver’s licenses, background screenings, and legal eligibility to possess firearms.

Working Conditions and Position Expectations
This position may require regular work at an off-campus shooting range and other outdoor locations; occasional evening and weekend work; and travel to meetings, training events, conferences, or partner activities. The employee must be able to work in varied outdoor conditions and safely handle, transport, inspect, and arrange shooting sports equipment and supplies consistent with the essential functions of the position. Any requirements related to a valid driver’s license, background screening, eligibility to possess firearms, lifting, or other physical demands will be established in accordance with Auburn University policies and applicable law.

About the College and Auburn University
The College of Forestry, Wildlife and Environment (cfwe.auburn.edu) is a national and international leader in forestry, wildlife, and natural resources programs and the flagship institution of Alabama’s $40+ billion-plus forest, wildlife, and natural resources-related enterprises, a significant component of the state’s economy and employment. The College is home to eight undergraduate degree programs and nearly 500 undergraduate students. Graduate student enrollment exceeds 175 students, and the College includes 49 research, teaching, and extension faculty.

Auburn University (www.auburn.edu) is one of the nation’s premier land, sea, and space-grant institutions, with an enrollment of more than 30,000 graduate and undergraduate students. The University is nationally recognized for its commitment to academic excellence and community engagement, positive work environment, flourishing student life programs, and beautiful campus. Auburn is located in east-central Alabama, approximately 100 miles southwest of Atlanta, Georgia; southeast of Birmingham, Alabama; and approximately 60 miles from the state capital, Montgomery.

·         A cover letter addressing the candidate’s interest and experience relevant to the responsibilities of the position;
·         A current curriculum vitae or résumé;
·         A vision statement for the shooting sports program;
·         Unofficial copies of academic transcripts and relevant certifications; and
·         The names and contact information of at least three professional references.



Contact
Mark D. Smith
334-844-8099

Description
 *Applications are reviewed on a rolling-basis and applications may close before the deadline.

USDA Forest Service Office/Lab and Location: A fellowship opportunity is available with the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) Forest Service (FS) within the Forest Service Northern Research Station (NRS) located in Grand Rapids, Minnesota.

At the heart of the USDA Forest Service's mission is their purpose. Everything they do is intended to help sustain forests and grasslands for present and future generations. Why? Because their stewardship work supports nature in sustaining life. This is the purpose that drives the agency’s mission and motivates their work across the agency. It’s been there from the agency’s very beginning, and it still drives them. To advance the mission and serve their purpose, the USDA Forest Service balances the short and long-term needs of people and nature by: working in collaboration with communities and our partners; providing access to resources and experiences that promote economic, ecological, and social vitality; connecting people to the land and one another; and delivering world-class science, technology and land management.

Research Project: Knowledge of soil frost and consequent effects on water availability over time is important to forest management, timber operations, and water supply for rural communities. Despite overall warmer annual air temperature, northern Minnesota forest soils are freezing longer and deeper, with expected effects on ecosystem water availability related to forest cover and soil type. Cumulative effects have strong implications for forest management throughout the year, particularly during winter when considerable harvesting and removal of merchantable timber occurs, but also during summer when water availability to support tree growth depends on prior winter conditions. You will be a part of research on soil conditions that differ from past decades and consequences for forest operations and ecosystem productivity as winter weather changes in northern Minnesota. You will gain experience with and knowledge of analyzing empirical data from long-term field studies and implementing models to simulate soil frost formation under a range of scenarios. You will be mentored by a Forest Service Research Hydrologist and engage with scientists and colleagues inside and outside the USDA Forest Service. 

Learning Objectives: Under the guidance of a mentor, you will have the opportunity to learn to: 

Describe soil frost formation and dissipation, and the relevance to forest hydrology and landscape level water availability;
Evaluate and interpret long-term ecosystem data sets;
Analyze data through model development/implementation and interpretation of results.
Apply steps to disseminate research through the preparation of a manuscript for journal publication.
Mentor: The mentor for this opportunity is Stephen Sebestyen ([email removed]). If you have questions about the nature of the research, please contact the mentor.

Description
Pacific States Marine Fisheries Commission is recruiting candidates to fill the role of a Fishery Biologist 2 to work closely with U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) researchers at the Klamath Falls Field Station (KFFS) on juvenile suckers. This is a full-time, benefits eligible position with an anticipated start date of January 4th, 2027.
 
The USGS Klamath Falls Field Station (KFFS) conducts research on rare and imperiled fishes in the Klamath Basin, helping managers make informed decisions about resource use in a sensitive arid ecosystem. 
The incumbent would join a collaborative team of biologists and data managers, with room to make meaningful parts of the project your own. The USGS Klamath Falls Field Station team has been tracking individual Lost River and Shortnose suckers — two long-lived, endangered fish species — for more than two decades, and is growing an acoustic telemetry program to better understand their movement and survival. Spend your summers doing hands-on juvenile sucker fieldwork, then pivot the rest of the year into acoustic telemetry, genetics, and data analysis. What makes this data special is the ability to track individual suckers across their entire life cycle — this role focuses on the juvenile piece of that story, working to understand why so few juveniles survive to join the adult population. A strong candidate for this position would have a master’s degree or doctorate in fisheries biology, ecology, or a closely related field, supplemented by relevant professional, research, or postdoctoral experience. We're looking for someone who's a strong team player with the grit to see a project through to completion. 
 
Please pay close attention to the required application materials and the closing disclaimer in the below sections.
 
Closing Disclaimer:
PSMFC will not accept resumes or cover letters for any position once the job announcement has been removed from the Careers Page. PSMFC will begin reviewing submitted applications the week of November 16, 2026 and may begin interviewing as soon as the week of November 23, 2026. PSMFC reserves the right to remove a job announcement at any time for any reason or close the position prior to the posted close date once a sufficient number of applicants have been received.             

Group Definition: Fishery Biologists use professional knowledge and competence in the science of fishery biology to perform work: (a) developing, conserving, propagating, managing, and administering fishery resources; (b) evaluating the impact of construction projects and other socioeconomic activities that present potential or actual adverse effects on fishery resources and their habitat; and (c) producing and managing aquatic resources in their natural habitat and/or within facilities and systems that have been constructed for their benefit and public use.

Position/Project Specifics: This position offers an opportunity to contribute to long-term research supporting the recovery of endangered Lost River and Shortnose suckers in the Klamath Basin. Working with the USGS KFFS, you'll help researchers better understand sucker survival, movement, and habitat use, information that supports species recovery and water-management decisions. The station's long-term monitoring program tracks individual fish using Passive Integrated Transponder tag (PIT-tag) and is expanding its acoustic telemetry efforts to better understand fish movement and survival. This research provides a valuable foundation for connecting juvenile recruitment, adult survival, and lake conditions to the broader challenge of sucker recovery.
The incumbent’s primary responsibility will be coordinating a single research project centered on juvenile sucker monitoring, working as part of an established and collaborative research team. The project involves standardized field sampling, aging, and genetic species identification of juvenile suckers across Upper Klamath Lake and/or Clear Lake Reservoir, which occurs primarily during the summer field season; field leads carry out the majority of hands-on field sampling, while this position coordinates the broader research effort, including data management support, analysis, and reporting of results following the field season.
Outside of the juvenile sampling season, this position will support a variety of other station needs as they arise, depending on current priorities. This additional work may include: supporting acoustic telemetry efforts, such as maintaining receiver arrays, assisting with tagging operations, and analyzing detection data as it comes in; contributing to writing and analysis on other station projects; scanning for PIT tags at piscivorous bird colonies; and supporting adult sucker sampling in the spring. The specific mix of additional work will vary by season and station need.
 
Essential Functions: PSMFC is seeking a Fisheries Biologist 2 who is comfortable performing most of the tasks below. The ideal candidate will have experience performing independent field research and monitoring.  
At the lower end of the range, Fishery Biologists 2:   
Follows existing protocols for fish health screenings; conduct tissue sample collection, bacterial testing and analyses, blood collection and analyses, parasite identification, and necropsies on experimental fish populations. Recommend modifications of existing research protocols. Design data collection forms and set up research databases for integration of data. Compile and analyze data for reports, prepare graphics, contribute to or write papers for peer-reviewed journals, and present research results at professional meetings. 
Develop age composition structures, stock assessments, escapement totals, harvest levels, run reconstruction frameworks, and/or run forecasts for designated fish species and stock. Evaluate and direct sampling efforts or reporting practices to best meet data requirements. Write memoranda and reports necessary for transfer of information to the appropriate individuals, agencies, and organizations. 
Plan, schedule, and conduct behavioral, physiological, morphological, and survival evaluations of hatchery and/or experimental fish populations. Oversee and assist with fish culture tasks for study purposes and recommend procedure variations. Write or contribute to papers and reports for publication, and compile reports on results of data collection and analysis. Prepare and deliver formal and informal presentations at seminars, meetings, etc. 
Plan, design, schedule, and conduct fish catch and effort surveys for marine fisheries. Utilize existing general sucker sampling protocols and determine modifications that address specific marine fisheries conditions or special fisheries.  Assist with database presentations of the data collected. Prepare reports and presentations as requested. Provide expertise in improvements to the design of sucker sampling methods 
Conduct limited physical and biological watershed, stream, and fish habitat assessments. Responsible for conducting data investigation and research, drafting technical report, database management, GIS for all physical and biological data, and survey and inventory results. Prepare, present, implement and update watershed assessment plans. 
Assist in writing contract proposals and progress reports. Assist in developing detailed contract specifications, task statements, quality of work criteria, and other specifications. 
Monitor budget expenses for projects, control purchasing, and manage equipment inventories. 
At the upper end of the range, the Fishery Biologist 2 has to: 

Use biological information to evaluate run profiles and habitat suitability in stocked streams within a major geographical area. Develop comprehensive management plans to insure preservation, protection, and enhancement of habitats. 
Plan, design and implement research studies on fish health and/or nutrition. Analyze and report biological and/or genetic information affecting future selection, rearing, and spawning activities. 
Prepare fish habitat measurement plans or management plans for a watershed or large geographic area. 
Diagnose various fish diseases or nutritional disorders in experimental populations or brood stock. Develop modifications to existing health protocols as well as experimental protocols. 
Write publishable reports of research and project findings. 
Knowledge Required by the Position:

Knowledge of fishery biology (including knowledge of catostomid). 
Knowledge of aquatic habitats. 
Knowledge of the scientific method. 
Knowledge of sampling protocols. 
Knowledge of Windows-based computer applications such as word processing, spreadsheets, e-mail, publishing software, presentation software, database software, topographic software, bibliographic software, and statistical analysis packages. 
Knowledge of technical writing protocols. 
Knowledge of advanced statistical analysis and mathematics. 
Additional Mandatory Skills :

Lift 40-50 lbs. 
Load boats on trailers 
Tow & maneuver trailers 
Electronic detection technol 
Fish ageing (scale, otolith, other) 
Fish species ID skills 
Valid driver’s license 
Specific software (spreadsheet, word processing, database management, GIS, statistical analysis, bibliographic) 
Ability to code in R or Python for data management and analysis. 
Oral communication skills  
Written communication skills

Hiking operate GPS

Physical Demands:

The work is sedentary with moderate walking between workstations and carrying folders, reports, and similar light loads.

Work Environment:

The work is performed in an office setting with adequate lighting, heating and ventilation. There are the normal risks of an office environment. 

PSMFC is an EEO/AAP employer. We maintain a drug free workplace.


Qualifications
Minimum Qualification Requirements:
A range of education and experience may be presented.

At the lower end of the range, candidates must present successful completion of a full 4-year course of study in an accredited college or university leading to a bachelor’s or higher degree that included a major in biological science with at least 6 semester hours in aquatic subjects and at least 12 semester hours in the animal sciences. In addition to the undergraduate degree requirement, candidates for positions at the lower end of the range must also present 1 year of Specialized Experience** OR 2 years of progressively higher graduate education leading to a master’s degree in fisheries biology, ecology, or a closely related field.

At the upper end of therange, in addition to the undergraduate course of study described above, candidates must also must present one year of Specialized Experience** OR 3 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a Ph. D. degree or equivalent doctoral degree in fields directly related to the position being filled. An equivalent combination of experience and education is also qualifying.

**Specialized Experience is experience that equips the applicant with the knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform successfully the duties of the position and is typically in or related to the work of the position being filled. To be creditable, specialized experience must have been equivalent to at least the next lower level in the normal line of progression for the position being filled.

To work with USGS Data Systems, the Candidate must also meet the below minimum requirements  
Federal System Access: Must meet federal eligibility requirements to access and utilize federal data systems.  
Citizenship & Residency: Due to federal security mandates, this position requires U.S. citizenship or lawful permanent residency (Green Card holder) maintained for a minimum of three consecutive years.  
Background Investigation: Position is contingent upon the successful completion of a comprehensive federal agency background investigation.  
Driving Clearance: Offers of employment for positions located in Oregon are contingent upon supplying and clearing an MVR check. The selected candidate must provide PSMFC with a copy of their 3-Year Oregon Motor Vehicle Record (MVR) and are responsible for all associated DMV fees.

Include a brief summary of each product (no more than one page per product) describing the product, your role in producing it, and its relevance to management or decision-making.

·       Workers’ compensation and applicable payroll coverage

·       Access to university research resources and infrastructure

Position Description
            The McMillan Lab at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln is seeking a motivated M.S. student to join a collaborative research project evaluating grazing and herbicide-based restoration strategies in Nebraska’s eastern saline wetlands. The student will be based in the Department of Agronomy and Horticulture and mentored by Dr. Nic McMillan.
            Eastern Nebraska’s saline wetlands support distinctive plant communities and provide habitat for a variety of wetland-associated wildlife. However, many of these wetlands have been degraded by invasive vegetation, altered disturbance regimes, hydrologic changes, and surrounding land use. Land managers need practical strategies that reduce invasive vegetation, promote native wetland plants, and create heterogeneous vegetation conditions across these landscapes to support both game and non-game wildlife species.
            The broader project will evaluate the effects of focal grazing, targeted herbicide application, and the combination of grazing and herbicide on plant community composition, vegetation structure, habitat heterogeneity, and cattle use of saline-wetland landscapes. The project is intended to connect fundamental questions about herbivory and vegetation heterogeneity with the applied restoration and management needs of conservation partners in Nebraska, which include: the Lower Platte South Natural Resource District (NRD), the City of Lincoln, and the Nebraska Game and Parks Commission, among others.
            The student will develop an M.S. thesis within the broader objectives of the funded project. Potential thesis directions include plant community responses to restoration treatments, changes in vegetation structure and heterogeneity, cattle distribution within saline-wetland landscapes, relationships between livestock use and vegetation conditions, or interactions between grazing and invasive-plant management. The specific thesis questions will be developed collaboratively based on project needs, the student’s interests, and the suitability of the resulting data.
            Field research will be conducted in eastern Nebraska saline wetlands in collaboration with conservation professionals, land managers, agency personnel, and other project partners. The work will integrate field-based vegetation measurements with information on livestock distribution and management treatments. GPS collars and virtual-fencing technology may be used to monitor and manage cattle distribution within focal treatment areas.

Primary Responsibilities
·       Conduct field sampling of plant species composition, vegetation structure, and related habitat characteristics in eastern Nebraska saline wetlands
·       Assist with the implementation and documentation of grazing and herbicide treatments
·       Assist with the deployment (i.e., animal fitting), maintenance, and retrieval of GPS collars and virtual-fencing equipment used to monitor and manage cattle distribution
·       Monitor field treatments and equipment during the growing season
·       Organize, document, and quality-check vegetation, treatment, and livestock-location data
·       Analyze ecological and spatial data using appropriate statistical methods
·       Evaluate treatment effects on plant communities, vegetation structure, habitat heterogeneity, and livestock use
·       Work collaboratively with university researchers, land managers, conservation organizations, agency personnel, and other project partners
·       Develop and complete an M.S. thesis within the broader objectives of the project
·       Present research findings at statewide, regional, national and international professional or scientific meetings—e.g., Society for Range Management, Ecological Society of America, The Wildlife Society
·       Contribute to reports, management recommendations, and manuscripts for peer-reviewed publication

            This position is well suited for a student interested in grazing ecology, wetland restoration, plant community ecology, invasive plant management, plant–herbivore interactions, landscape heterogeneity, and applied conservation. The project provides an opportunity to conduct research that advances ecological understanding while directly informing management of one of Nebraska’s most distinctive and imperiled ecosystem types.

            The successful applicant will join a collaborative research environment focused on large-herbivore ecology, landscape heterogeneity, biodiversity, and the ecological consequences of spatially variable disturbance. The student will also gain experience working with land managers and conservation partners and translating ecological findings into practical management recommendations.

Eligibility Requirements
·       Must hold a bachelor’s degree by the position start date
·       Must meet admission requirements for the appropriate M.S. degree program at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln
·       Must be admitted to a specific graduate-degree objective and enrolled for credit during the fall and spring semesters
·       Must maintain good academic standing throughout the appointment
·       Must be eligible to work in the United States
·       Must be available to begin the assistantship no later than January 11, 2027 -- Preferred start by January 4, 2027.
·       Must possess a valid driver’s license or be able to obtain one before beginning fieldwork
·       Must be willing and able to travel to field sites and conduct fieldwork under hot, humid, muddy, and otherwise variable conditions
·       Must be able to work independently and cooperatively as part of a field and research team

Preferred Qualifications
·       B.S. degree in ecology, rangeland science, wildlife biology, natural resources, agronomy, environmental science, plant science, animal science, or a related field
·       Interest in grazing ecology, wetland restoration, plant community ecology, invasive species management, or plant–herbivore interactions
·       Experience conducting vegetation, wetland, rangeland, livestock, or wildlife fieldwork
·       Experience working with cattle or in livestock-production systems
·       Familiarity with R, GIS, GPS data, spatial analysis, or ecological data management
·       Strong organizational skills and careful attention to data quality
·       Effective written and oral communication skills
·       Ability to communicate and work professionally with researchers, land managers, agricultural producers, agency personnel, and conservation partners


            Previous experience with livestock, wetlands, R, GIS, or animal-movement data is helpful but not required. Applicants do not need to possess all preferred qualifications. Students with relevant transferable experience, a strong interest in the research, and a demonstrated willingness to learn are encouraged to apply.

Application Instructions
To apply, please submit the following materials to Dr. Nic McMillan at [email removed]. Use “Saline Wetlands M.S. Application – [Last Name]” in the email subject line.

1.     Cover letter describing your interest in the position, relevant experience, research interests, and professional goals
2.     Curriculum vitae or résumé
3.     Unofficial transcripts from all colleges and universities attended
4.     Contact information for two professional or academic references

            Applications received by November 20, 2026, will receive full consideration. Review may begin as applications are received and will continue until the position is filled. The selected applicant must also apply to and be admitted by the appropriate graduate program at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln.

Description
Quantitative Ecology Postdoctoral Positions

The University of Minnesota seeks three postdoctoral researchers to work collaboratively with Drs. John Fieberg, Gretchen Hansen, and Jake Walsh on funded projects examining the ecosystem effects of invasive aquatic plants and their management. Together, the projects will evaluate the benefits, costs, and ecological tradeoffs of invasive aquatic plant treatments and support management decisions under uncertainty.
 
The three researchers will work together, share methods and ecological expertise, and collaborate with managers, practitioners, and other partners. Each will have primary research responsibilities, with opportunities to contribute across projects based on their expertise and interests. The positions offer opportunities for collaborative mentorship across the three faculty labs and the Minnesota Aquatic Invasive Species Research Center.


Research areas

The group will address three connected areas:

Causal effects of invasive plants and their management: Develop and apply causal inference methods to estimate ecological effects from observational lake and management data.
Aquatic plant responses and adaptive management: Analyze statewide data from more than 6,000 aquatic plant surveys and hundreds of management treatments to evaluate effects on native and invasive plants. Develop practical, statistically sound approaches to guide future monitoring.
Decision analysis and native species conservation: Work with partners to compare management alternatives, evaluate tradeoffs for invasive plant control and native fish and plant conservation, and identify uncertainties that matter most to management decisions.
Qualifications

Required

A PhD in ecology, fisheries, aquatic science, statistics, applied mathematics, decision science, natural resource management, or a related field by the start date.
Demonstrated experience conducting quantitative analyses and developing or applying statistical or decision models.
Ability to lead analytical work independently and collaborate effectively across disciplines.
Strong organizational and written and oral communication skills.

Preferred

We welcome applicants with experience in one or more of the following areas:

Causal inference using observational data.
Structured decision making, decision modeling, sensitivity analysis, or value of information.
State-space models or hierarchical Bayesian models.
Aquatic ecology, aquatic plant biology, or aquatic invasive species management.
Ecological survey design, occupancy modeling, or community analysis.
Partner engagement, meeting facilitation, or collaborative research with management organizations.
Teaching, training, or student mentorship.

We seek complementary strengths across the three hires. Applicants need not meet every desired qualification and should describe their strongest areas of expertise and interests in collaboration. We welcome candidates who will contribute to a supportive and inclusive research environment.

How To Apply

Applications must be submitted online. To be considered for this position, please search for Job ID 376741 on the University of Minnesota's job board. If you have any questions, feel free to reach out to Dr. John Fieberg ([email removed]), Dr. Gretchen Hansen ([email removed]) or Dr. Jake Walsh ([email removed]).

Prepare reports, audits, and documentation for internal reviews, regulatory submissions, and leadership briefings

2+ years in environmental due diligence, natural resources, or construction-phase compliance
Experience with delineations, habitat assessments, or threatened and endangered species surveys
Experience working with design teams, construction teams, or both, on active projects

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

Bachelor’s degree (Master’s preferred) in environmental science, ecology, biology, environmental engineering, natural resources, or a related field

Ability to multi-task, prioritize multiple projects at once, and follow through with a project until completion with minimal oversight

Experience using Windows operating systems and Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook)

Description
The Freshwater Community Ecology Lab at The Ohio State University (OSU) is seeking a postdoctoral researcher to investigate how fish movement influences the effectiveness of mechanical control strategies for invasive species. This position will focus on building simulation models for smallmouth bass in the Upper Colorado River working with collaborators from the US Geological Survey and the Upper Colorado River Endangered Fish Recovery Program. The researcher will evaluate how varying hypotheses regarding fish movement interact with mechanical removal scenarios to best control smallmouth bass populations.

This researcher will also have opportunities to get involved with and potentially lead other projects in the Freshwater Community Ecology Lab, including projects focused on stream fish community dynamics, movement, estimating demographic rates, and identifying drivers of population dynamics in a wide range of systems including wadable streams in Ohio, the Colorado River, and Lake Erie.

Key Responsibilities
• Develop quantitative demographic models to test population sensitivity under diverse removal and movement scenarios.
• Translate model outputs into actionable management insight for agency partners.
• Work as part of a collaborative research team
• Lead manuscript drafting for peer-reviewed journals, prepare reports, and present findings at regional and national conferences

Qualifications
Required:
• Ph.D. in Ecology, Fisheries Science, Quantitative Biology, or a closely related field
• Strong publication and presentation record relative to career stage
• Excellent communication skills and comfort working with collaborative groups
Preferred:
• Strong background in quantitative ecology, population modeling, and simulation tools
• Prior experience working collaboratively on research projects

About the Environment
The successful applicant will join the Freshwater Community Ecology Lab under supervision of Dr. Lindsey Bruckerhoff (https://u.osu.edu/bruckerhofflab/ ). The Freshwater Community Ecology Lab is part of OSU’s Aquatic Ecology Laboratory (AEL), a collaborative and dynamic research facility within the Department of Evolution, Ecology, and Organismal Biology. The AEL brings together faculty, postdocs, graduate students, and technicians focused on management-driven freshwater research. Learn more about our lab community and research facilities at ael.osu.edu.

Full time benefits include Medical, Dental, Vision, 401K, and other possible benefits as provided.  Benefits are subject to change with or without notice.

Researcher III Responsibilities Include: 
Conduct advanced molecular biology research in accordance with established standard operating procedures (SOPs).
Extract, purify, quantify, and assess the quality of DNA and RNA from biological and environmental samples.
Perform PCR, quantitative PCR (qPCR), gel electrophoresis, and related molecular laboratory procedures.
Maintain and support research involving cell cultures and cell lines.
Design, optimize, and troubleshoot primers, assays, and molecular biology protocols.
Collect, prepare, evaluate, verify, and process biological and environmental samples.
Prepare laboratory reagents, chemical solutions, and mixtures in accordance with SOPs and laboratory safety requirements.
Perform laboratory QA/QC activities and promptly identify, document, troubleshoot, and communicate technical or data-management issues.
Train or assist laboratory personnel in approved laboratory procedures and SOPs.
Operate, maintain, and troubleshoot core laboratory equipment, including pipettors, thermocyclers, spectrophotometers, centrifuges, dewars, and gas cylinders.
Maintain inventories of laboratory chemicals, reagents, supplies, and equipment; identify and communicate procurement needs.
Coordinate shipment and receipt of samples, supplies, chemicals, and laboratory equipment.
Support laboratory safety assessments, laboratory-readiness checks, PPE availability, and personnel training compliance.
Maintain complete, accurate, and organized laboratory notebooks, field notes, data sheets, training logs, and digital and hard-copy research records.
Compile, tabulate, analyze, summarize, and prepare experimental data for reports, presentations, graphics, and other research products.
Conduct scientific literature reviews and synthesize findings for ongoing research projects.
Support proposals, reports, presentations, outreach materials, scientific meetings, internal review systems, workshops, and collaborator communications.
Assist with planning and conducting fieldwork, including equipment preparation, supply organization, datasheet development, instrument calibration, and logistics coordination.
Submit monthly and as-requested progress reports covering technical, operational, administrative, and data-management activities. 
Performs other job-related duties as assigned

Master’s degree in biology, molecular biology, genetics, ecology, environmental science, wildlife science, or another relevant scientific field required.
At least five years of relevant laboratory experience in an academic, government, or professional research setting required.
Demonstrated experience with most of the following required molecular laboratory skills:
DNA and RNA extraction, purification, and quantification
PCR and qPCR
Gel electrophoresis
Cell culture or cell-line management
Primer and assay design/optimization
Molecular biology protocol troubleshooting
Working knowledge of standard genetic laboratory methods, laboratory software, documentation practices, and SOP-driven processes required.
Experience with genomic data, genetic data, transcriptomics, and/or cell lines preferred.
Ability to work independently with limited supervision while following established technical, safety, and operational procedures.
Strong organization, time-management, and multitasking skills to support multiple projects and scientists.
Ability to maintain records that support data integrity, reproducibility, traceability, continuity, and archival requirements.
Experience compiling, organizing, manipulating, and summarizing scientific data; familiarity with tabular and graphical data-representation software.
Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to translate laboratory work into reports and other narrative products.
Active USAccess clearance/credential or ability to obtain and maintain required access credentials.
Current First Aid, CPR, and Bloodborne Pathogens certifications required before or upon entry.
Ability to complete required training, including laboratory safety, GHS classification, Quality Management System training, IT security, and other task-specific courses.
Ability to work full time on-site in Gainesville, FL, averaging 40 hours per week; schedules may vary during fieldwork.
Ability to travel periodically, including possible extended field trips, when approved and funded.
Ability to meet physical and environmental requirements, including prolonged sitting, standing, stooping, bending, and computer work; lifting and moving laboratory equipment or supplies up to 50 pounds; exposure to temperature extremes; and handling hazardous or irritant chemicals.

Description
In cooperation with the National Park Service, the Great Basin Institute (GBI) is recruiting a Cultural Resources Emergency Management Technician to work cooperatively with National Park Service staff at the four NPS sites in Contra Costa County, CA including: Eugene O’Neill National Historic Site (EUON) in Danville, John Muir National Historic Site (JOMU) in Martinez, Port Chicago Naval Magazine National Memorial (POCH) in Concord, and Rosie the Riveter/WWII Home Front National Historical Park (RORI) in Richmond.

This project entails developing three Museum Collection Emergency Response Plans (MCEOP) and three Museum Fire chapters to be included in the parks’ Structural Fire Management Plans (one of each plan for JOMU, EUON/POCH, and RORI). Working under the direction of the Museum Curator, plan templates, professional survey assessment results, and information about current park practices will be provided to aid plan development. Established emergency response supply caches will be inventoried and evaluated and the research associate will provide recommendations for additional supplies based on threats assessed in the MCEOPs. The research associate will conduct staff training sessions about emergency supply cache locations, supply use, and prescribed emergency response procedures as outlined in the finalized plans.


Timeline:
Mid-January 2027 through September 2027, 33 week appointment;
Part time (16 hours/ week);
Schedule: Two eight hour days a week.

Location:
This position is primarily located in the administrative headquarters for Rosie the Riveter/WWII Home Front National Historical Park in Richmond, CA. Incorporated on August 3, 1905, Richmond has a rich history and played a significant role during World War II on the home front. Known for its central location in the Bay Area, just 16 miles northeast of San Francisco, which makes it a hub for transportation with two Interstate freeways, railroads, a deepwater shipping port, and a combined BART and AMTRAK station. The yearly temperature typically varies from a low of 42°F to a high of 77°F, rarely dipping below 35°F or exceeding 87°F.

Occasional same-day site visits within office hours to John Muir National Historic Site in Martinez, CA and Eugene O’Neill National Historic Site in Danville, CA (both located in Contra Costa County and within 30 miles of Richmond) will be required.


Compensation and Benefits:

Wage: $36.97 hourly;

Benefits: 

Sick Leave;
Access to Pro Deals

Please note that we will be interviewing candidates in late October 2026

QUALIFICATIONS:

Minimum requirements:
Successful completion of a Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution that includes major study in a field directly related to museum studies. Additionally, experience or training which includes topics such as: museum collection management, emergency planning, emergency response and salvage, Incident Command System, risk assessment, museum-specific hazards, fire safety, and physical security procedures. Demonstrates excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills and the ability to work independently. 

Preferred:
In addition to the above, preference is given to an individual with a master’s degree from an information science or public history program with an emphasis in museum collection management. Familiarity with past, current, and emerging trends in the fields of heritage protection and disaster preparedness. 


TO APPLY
Please submit an up-to-date resume, a one-page cover letter that details your interest in the position, and any qualifications not fully outlined in your resume, and contact information for three professional references. Qualified applicants will be contacted to schedule an interview. 


PHYSICAL DEMANDS  
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable employees with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit, use hands, stand, walk, bend, and have specific vision abilities to include close and distance vision, and ability to adjust focus working with computer business equipment and other job/industry specific equipment. The noise level in the work environment is usually low.

The overall nature of the Indoor position is sedentary, requiring some physical effort and occasional exertion. There is occasional exposure to environmental conditional such as heat, cold and temperature changes.


NOTE:  This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive. Employees may perform other related duties as negotiated to meet the organization's ongoing needs. All offers of employment are contingent upon the successful completion of a pre-employment background check.

Disclaimer: Although the organization has attempted to accurately and thoroughly describe this position, GBI reserves the right to change the same, including to change, add to or subtract from the duties outlined, within the sole discretion of the organization, at any time, with or without advance notice.
