Description
Pacific States Marine Fisheries Commission is recruiting candidates to fill the role of a Fishery Biologist 2 to work closely with U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) researchers at the Klamath Falls Field Station (KFFS) on adult fish monitoring. This is a full-time, benefits-eligible position with an anticipated start date of January 4th, 2026.
 
Please review required application materials and the closing disclaimer in the below sections.
 
Closing Disclaimer:
PSMFC will not accept resumes or cover letters for any position once the job announcement has been removed from the Careers Page. PSMFC will begin reviewing submitted applications the week of November 16, 2026 and may begin interviewing as soon as the week of November 23, 2026. PSMFC reserves the right to remove a job announcement at any time for any reason or close the position prior to the posted close date once a sufficient number of applicants have been received.
 
The USGS KFFS has been tracking individual Lost River and Shortnose suckers — two long-lived, endangered fish species — for more than two decades.
The incumbent would be leading the field logistics behind adult sucker monitoring, from running boats and maintaining Passive Integrated Transponder tag (PIT-tag) detection equipment to scheduling and coordinating field crews through back-to-back spring and fall field seasons. You'll also get exposure to juvenile sucker work and fin-ray aging and genetic sampling across both life stages, giving you a rare full-life-cycle view of an endangered species most biologists never get. If you're someone who's at your best running field operations, keeping equipment and crews moving, and wants real ownership over how a season comes together, we'd like to hear from you.
 
Group Definition:  Fishery Biologists use professional knowledge and competence in the science of fishery biology to perform work: (a) developing, conserving, propagating, managing, and administering fishery resources; (b) evaluating the impact of construction projects and other socioeconomic activities that present potential or actual adverse effects on fishery resources and their habitat; and (c) producing and managing aquatic resources in their natural habitat and/or within facilities and systems that have been constructed for their benefit and public use.

Position/Project Specifics:
This position offers the opportunity to contribute to research on rare and imperiled fishes in the Klamath Basin, generating information that helps managers make informed decisions about resource use in a sensitive arid ecosystem. You'll work within a long-term research program that has tracked endangered Lost River and Shortnose suckers for decades using PIT tags as part of a capture-recapture effort, while contributing to an expanding acoustic telemetry program investigating seasonal movement, survival, and habitat use. Through this work, you'll help connect adult survival, juvenile recruitment, and lake conditions to sucker recovery actions and water-management decisions in the Basin.
 
The incumbent’s primary responsibility will be coordinating a single research project centered on adult sucker monitoring, working as part of an established and collaborative research team. The project involves standardized field sampling, aging, and genetic species identification of adult and juvenile suckers across Upper Klamath Lake and/or Clear Lake Reservoir, which occurs primarily during the spring and late fall field season. This position also manages and coordinates field crew schedules to install and maintain remote PIT tag detection equipment and seasonal field sampling events, and manages day-to-day maintenance on boats and vehicles to ensure continuous operation and availability to accommodate the busy field schedule.
 
Outside of the adult sampling season, this position will support a variety of other station needs as they arise, depending on current priorities This additional work may include: supporting acoustic telemetry efforts, such as maintaining receiver arrays, assisting with tagging operations, and analyzing detection data as it comes in; contributing to writing and analysis on other station projects; scanning for PIT tags at piscivorous bird colonies; and supporting juvenile sucker sampling in the summer months when needed. The specific mix of additional work will vary by season and station need. The ideal candidate will have experience leading or co-leading field crew, have work experience with acoustic telemetry. 
 
Essential Functions: 
 
At the lower end of the range, Fishery Biologists 2: 
Follow existing protocols for fish health screenings; conduct tissue sample collection, bacterial testing and analyses, blood collection and analyses, parasite identification, and necropsies on experimental fish populations. Recommend modifications of existing research protocols. Design data collection forms and set up research databases for integration of data. Compile and analyze data for reports, prepare graphics, contribute to or write papers for peer-reviewed journals, and present research results at professional meetings. 
Develop age composition structures, stock assessments, escapement totals, harvest levels, run reconstruction frameworks, and/or run forecasts for designated fish species and stock. Evaluate and direct sampling efforts or reporting practices to best meet data requirements. Write memoranda and reports necessary for transfer of information to the appropriate individuals, agencies, and organizations. 
Plan, schedule, and conduct behavioral, physiological, morphological, and survival evaluations of hatchery and/or experimental fish populations. Oversee and assist with fish culture tasks for study purposes and recommend procedure variations. Write or contribute to papers and reports for publication, and compile reports on results of data collection and analysis. Prepare and deliver formal and informal presentations at seminars, meetings, etc. 
Plan, design, schedule, and conduct fish catch and effort surveys. Utilize existing general sucker survey protocols and determine modifications that address specific marine fisheries conditions or special fisheries. . Assist with database presentations of the data collected. Prepare reports and presentations as requested. Provide expertise in improvements to the design of sucker sampling methods. 
Conduct limited physical and biological watershed, stream, and fish habitat assessments. Responsible for conducting data investigation and research, drafting technical report, database management, GIS for all physical and biological data, and survey and inventory results. Prepare, present, implement and update assessment plans. 
Assist in writing contract proposals and progress reports. Assist in developing detailed contract specifications, task statements, quality of work criteria, and other specifications. 
Monitor budget expenses for projects, control purchasing, and manage equipment inventories.
At the upper end of the range, the Fishery Biologist 2:

Use biological information to evaluate run profiles and habitat suitability in stocked streams within a major geographical area. Develop comprehensive management plans to ensure preservation, protection, and enhancement of habitats. 
Plan, design and implement research studies on fish health and/or nutrition. Analyze and report biological and/or genetic information affecting future selection, rearing, and spawning activities. 
Prepare fish habitat measurement plans or management plans for a watershed or large geographic area. 
Diagnose various fish diseases or nutritional disorders in experimental populations or brood stock. Develop modifications to existing health protocols as well as experimental protocols. 
Write publishable reports of research and project findings. 
Knowledge Required by the Position:

Knowledge of fishery biology (including knowledge of catostomid). 
Knowledge of aquatic habitats. 
Knowledge of the scientific method. 
Knowledge of sampling protocols. 
Knowledge of Windows-based computer applications such as word processing, spreadsheets, e-mail, publishing software, presentation software, database software, topographic software, bibliographic software, and statistical analysis packages. 
Knowledge of technical writing protocols. 
Knowledge of advanced statistical analysis and mathematics. 
Additional Mandatory/Desirable Skills:  

Load boats on trailers  
Tow & maneuver trailers 
Fish species ID skills  
Oral communication skills 
Specific software spreadsheet, word processing, database management, GIS, statistical analysis, bibliographic 
Fish species ID skills  
Oral communication skills 
Valid driver’s license 
Written communication skills 
Additional Desirable Skills:  

Able to swim 
Experience with acoustic telemetry and/or PIT-tag technologies, including maintenance of equipment  
Snorkeling 
Lift 40-50 lbs. 
Electronic detection technol. 
Hiking 
CPR/First Aid 
Using fish key 
Fish ageing (scale, otolith, other) 
Electrofishing-boat 
Operate trap/weir 
Operate nets (seine, gill, etc.) 
Electrofishing-backpack 
Operate motorized boats 
Literature search/review 
Operate GPS  
Physical Environment: Demands generally range from sedentary to moderate --where there is walking, climbing stairs and ladders, reaching, lifting, bending, or extended periods of standing. Some Fishery Biologists in this range have rigorous physical demands where they must be able to handle buckets of water or gear weighing from 40 - 50 pounds, engage in long daily periods of hiking, camp out for extended periods, or maintain footing in fast-moving water. 

 

Work Environment: Some work is performed in an office setting with adequate lighting, heating and ventilation. Some work may be performed in a laboratory setting which exposes the biologist to odors, chemicals, fish blood, and molds. The employee must use safety precautions including MSDS, gloves, hood, and eye protection. Some employees may work on narrow, elevated walkways and platforms that are over or adjacent to water. Field work involves exposure to all types of weather, slippery rocks or docks, trails, irregular terrain, insects, poison oak, rough or fast-moving water, or cold water temperatures. Work at high elevations or aboard boats may be required. 

PSMFC is an EEO/AAP employer. We maintain a drug free workplace.

Qualifications
Minimum Qualification Requirements:
A range of education and experience may be presented. At the lower end of the range, candidates must present successful completion of a full 4-year course of study in an accredited college or university leading to a bachelor’s or higher degree that included a major in biological science with at least 6 semester hours in aquatic subjects and at least 12 semester hours in the animal sciences. In addition to the undergraduate degree requirement, candidates for positions at the lower end of the range must also present 1 year of Specialized Experience** OR 2 years of progressively higher graduate education leading to a master’s degree in fisheries biology, ecology, or a closely related field. 

At the upper end of the range, in addition to the undergraduate course of study described above, candidates must also present one year of Specialized Experience** OR 3 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a Ph. D. degree or equivalent doctoral degree in fields directly related to the position being filled. An equivalent combination of experience and education is also qualifying.

**Specialized Experience is experience that equips the applicant with the knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform successfully the duties of the position and is typically in or related to the work of the position being filled. To be creditable, specialized experience must have been equivalent to at least the next lower level in the normal line of progression for the position being filled.

To work with USGS Data Systems, the Candidate must also meet the below minimum requirements: 
Federal System Access: Must meet federal eligibility requirements to access and utilize federal data systems. 
Citizenship & Residency: Due to federal security mandates, this position requires U.S. citizenship or lawful permanent residency (Green Card holder) maintained for a minimum of three consecutive years. 
Background Investigation: Position is contingent upon the successful completion of a comprehensive federal agency background investigation. 
Driving Clearance: Offers of employment for positions located in Oregon are contingent upon supplying and clearing an MVR check. The selected candidate must provide PSMFC with a copy of their 3-Year Oregon Motor Vehicle Record (MVR) and are responsible for all associated DMV fees. 
Required Applications Materials 

Applications that do not include material listed under Requirement A and B will be considered incomplete. 

Requirement A – Resume: Resume (max 6 pages) that clearly demonstrates relevant education and experience. 
 

Requirement B – Cover Letter: Explain your interest in this specific position and how your background and career goals align with the role, the long-term sucker dataset, and the KFFS research program. The cover letter should communicate your interest in contributing to endangered species recovery and informing management decisions, rather than restating your CV.

NOW HIRING: Wildlife Biologist

The North Slope Borough (NSB) Department of Wildlife Management (DWM) (www.north-slope.org/departments/wildlife-management) is seeking a Wildlife Biologist. The NSB is a municipal government encompassing the entire North Slope of Alaska (88,000 mi2). Residents of the NSB live subsistence lifestyles and harvest a broad range of both terrestrial and marine animals, including caribou, polar bears, whales, seals, and walruses. 

This position has two primary roles:
(1) Document and analyze subsistence harvests of terrestrial and marine wildlife. The successful candidate will apply strong quantitative skills to survey design, data analysis, and reporting. Responsibilities include participating in harvest sampling; managing harvest data and its collection; providing technical support to staff; and working with and listening to local hunters and their communities.  (2) Conduct research to inform sustainable wildlife management decisions. The successful candidate will identify research questions that are relevant to terrestrial and marine wildlife species that are harvested for subsistence by North Slope residents; develop appropriate research methods; lead and participate in field data collection; analyze data; and prepare technical reports and scientific manuscripts. Across both roles, the candidate will collaborate and coordinate with colleagues from other agencies, industry, and local communities. To disseminate findings, the candidate will author peer-reviewed publications, present at professional conferences and meetings, and meet with local communities and other audiences.

Qualifications:  
A bachelor’s degree in biology or wildlife management and two years of experience. Although an advanced degree is not required, the strongest candidates will likely hold an advanced degree in biology, wildlife management, ecology, or a related field. Candidates should also demonstrate quantitative skills equivalent to those typically developed through graduate-level training at the M.S. or Ph.D. level. Successful applicants holding an advanced degree will receive a premium of 2% above base salary for an M.S. and 7% for a Ph.D. Preference will be given to applicants with: (1) a strong quantitative background; (2) proficiency with spreadsheets, databases, GIS, and R; (3) field experience in remote locations; (4) experience working with Indigenous peoples and related issues; (5) strong communication skills; (6) a demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively; and (7) enthusiasm for living and working in a remote but vibrant community.

Paid time off and 14 additional days of paid holiday leave per year.

Description
 Wildlife Opportunity 
This position offers an exciting and deeply rewarding opportunity to work directly with landowners to create high‑quality wildlife habitat and expand public hunting access on private lands. You will join a motivated, growing, and mission‑driven Private Lands Section within the Department’s Wildlife Division, where your work directly contributes to the success of the Private Land Initiative and the long‑term conservation of North Dakota’s wildlife resources. 
ND Game and Fish provides a challenging, fulfilling career with meaningful fieldwork, strong partnerships, and the chance to make a visible impact on the landscape. The Department also offers an exceptional benefits package, including 100% employer‑paid family health insurance, a comprehensive retirement plan, vacation and sick leave (including family sick leave), holiday pay, and other outstanding benefits. More information is available through Team ND Benefits. 
 The Community 
Dickinson is located on the “Western Edge of North Dakota”. Dickinson is a mid-sized community with various city amenities and offers access to outstanding outdoor recreational opportunities. The Little Missouri National Grasslands, Theodore Roosevelt National Park, and the North Dakota Badlands are just a short drive to the west. Lake Sakakawea is located approximately an hour and a half to the north and opportunities for upland and big game hunting opportunities are plentiful in the region. The position would be responsible for delivery of PLI programs in Billings, Dunn, Golden Valley, Slope and Stark counties. 
To learn more about living in North Dakota, visit https://findthegoodlife.com 
 Summary of Work 
The District Private Lands Biologist plays a key role in delivering, developing, and implementing the Private Lands Initiative, including the Department’s Habitat and Access Programs. Primary responsibilities include working one‑on‑one with private landowners to develop conservation agreements, specifically Private Land Open To Sportsmen (PLOTS) and habitat‑enhancement projects. 
The position requires close coordination with federal and state agricultural and wildlife agencies, conservation organizations, and other partners. Occasional operation of habitat‑management equipment is part of the role, along with conducting wildlife surveys, performing habitat assessments, and providing public outreach and information. 
 This is a hands‑on, field‑forward position where your work directly improves wildlife habitat, strengthens partnerships, and expands public hunting opportunities across North Dakota. 
 This is a salaried position and may require the individual to work long or extra hours, exceeding 40 hours per week, to complete tasks during specific periods throughout the year. 
 Minimum Qualifications: 
Requires a minimum of a Bachelor of Science degree in wildlife biology or wildlife management or closely related natural resource science degree and one year of professional work experience with a fish and wildlife agency or other conservation organization. A Master’s degree in a closely related field can substitute for one year of work experience. 
 The individual must possess well-developed communication skills, both oral and written, be highly responsible, be well organized and detail oriented. Must have the ability to work with private landowners, farmers/ranchers, other wildlife management professionals, wildlife groups, and the general public in a professional manner as a representative of the agency.  Must be self-motivated and adaptable to a fast-paced work environment with the ability to multi-task and balance many work responsibilities at once.  Must have a good working knowledge of Microsoft Office products (Outlook, Word and Excel). 
 The applicant must possess or be able to obtain a valid driver’s license. Must be able to travel; occasional overnight travel is required. 
 Requires successful completion of a background check. 
 Preferred Qualifications: 
Preference will be given to applicants with: 
 Experience using mapping software and/or interpreting maps and legal descriptions
Experience working with private landowners, farmers/ranchers
Experience developing or managing habitat projects
Experience delivering or administering conservation programs
Experience conducting wildlife surveys and/or habitat assessments
Experience responding to or managing human-wildlife conflicts
Active participation in hunting

 Applicants must complete the online application.  Applicants will be scored by their responses to the questionnaire questions.   
Applicants must also upload a Cover Letter describing how the applicant’s ability and experience relates to the Summary of Work.
Applicants must upload a current Resume that includes information to demonstrate how you meet the minimum qualifications as posted.
Applicants must attach a document listing at least 3 professional references.

Job Summary

The DNR is currently seeking (1) Conservation Easement Monitoring Specialist in our Duluth French River Office. This position conducts and coordinates conservation easement monitoring and reporting for the MNDNR Division of Fisheries and Wildlife. Primary duties include conducting baseline and monitoring surveys on conservation easements, communicating with landowners, preparing reports, and coordinating report approvals. Monitoring visits are conducted to evaluate compliance with easement terms and to assess ecological condition, including but not limited to identifying invasive species, assessing need for riparian vegetation management, erosion control, and stream channel or bank stabilization. Assessment data are analyzed to develop management guidance for habitat enhancement or restoration. 

Responsibilities Include:
 Monitor conservation easements held by the Division of Fisheries and Wildlife, including planning and scheduling baseline reporting and monitoring, preparing maps, and conducting field visits to ensure compliance with conservation easements.
Analyze ecological data to prioritize parcels for acquisition and coordinate with FAW land acquisition unit to acquire new conservation easements. 
Attend meetings of stewardship and enforcement working groups; providing input to increase efficiency and consistency and maintain/improve landowner relations.
Conduct habitat assessments on easements during routine inspections. Communicating relevant information to Area office so that it can inform management guidance for habitat improvement projects. 
Assess management issues within easement corridors, including identification of invasive species, needs for vegetation management, and needs related to stream geomorphology, channel stability, streambank erosion, and connectivity.

Description


The Roadside Ecology Center (REC) at Southern Illinois University Carbondale invites applications for a Lead Scientist/Coordinator to lead the scientific and compliance operations of the Center’s biological and wetland science team. The REC is a multi-institutional applied research and environmental compliance center operating under a long-term Intergovernmental Agreement with the Illinois Department of Transportation. The Center’s scientists conduct field surveys, threatened and endangered species assessments, and wetland evaluations across the southern third of Illinois to support IDOT’s environmental review obligations and the REC’s applied research program. The Lead Scientist/Coordinator receives and triages incoming IDOT taskings, assigns projects to scientists based on expertise and capacity, oversees the quality of compliance deliverables, and manages the team’s progression from field data to peer-reviewed publication.

Salary is competitive and commensurate with qualifications and experience, while also considering internal equity.



Examples of Duties

Triage incoming IDOT regulatory taskings: evaluate scope, urgency, and taxonomic requirements, assign projects to appropriate scientists, maintain an active project tracker, and ensure all compliance deliverables are completed accurately and on schedule. 
Provide direct scientific oversight of four Interdisciplinary Biologists and four Wetland Scientists and reviewing deliverables prior to IDOT submission. 
Manage the team’s applied research pipeline in coordination with the Director; facilitate the transition of compliance data streams into peer-reviewed publications by actively participating in manuscript preparation, providing scientific review, and co-authoring papers led by staff scientists. 
Establish and maintain field data collection standards that support regulatory compliance while also preserving the research utility of compliance datasets. 
Participate in field surveys as needed to support team capacity during peak workload periods, maintain multi-taxa proficiency across the biological and wetland disciplines represented on the team, and fill coverage gaps as needed across the southern Illinois service area. 
Monitor team capacity and geographic coverage needs across the southern Illinois service area; communicate proactively with the Director when tasking volume or staffing constraints require prioritization decisions. 
Represent the scientific team at quarterly state endangered species meetings, relevant interagency forums, and annual conferences; communicate field findings to IDOT and agency partners as directed by the Director.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:
PhD in ecology, wildlife biology, conservation biology, environmental science, or a closely related field 
4+ years of post-degree professional experience in applied ecological field work, environmental consulting, or natural resource management, including demonstrated responsibility for leading scientific teams or managing multi-species compliance project portfolios 
2+ years of direct supervisory experience managing field-based biological or environmental staff 
Demonstrated record of peer-reviewed publication in applied ecology or conservation biology, commensurate with the university-level Associate Scientist classification 
Broad field competency to sufficiently evaluate work quality and provide substantive scientific guidance to specialists on both the biological and wetland teams 
Working knowledge of Illinois and federal regulatory frameworks applicable to environmental review, including Sections 7 and 10 of the Endangered Species Act, Section 404 of the Clean Water Act, and Illinois state incidental take provisions 
Strong technical writing skills, with experience authoring or reviewing compliance reports and scientific manuscripts 
Valid driver’s license and willingness to travel regularly within southern Illinois and beyond
Preferred Qualifications:
Experience in transportation ecology, road ecology, or environmental compliance review for linear infrastructure
Direct experience working with state or federal transportation or natural resource agencies, including IDOT, IDNR, USACE, or USFWS 
Background in wildlife sampling protocols, with a particular interest in threatened and endangered species 
Background in wetland delineation and functional assessment methods or stream ecology 
Demonstrated experience mentoring scientists or graduate students toward peer-reviewed publication 
Familiarity with Illinois flora, fauna, and natural communities, particularly in the southern Illinois region
Required Documents: Please submit a letter of application, CV/Resume, Statement describing your research program in transportation and road ecology, and three references.

Contact: Brent Pease, [email removed]

We offer 200+ undergraduate degrees, minors and specializations, 79 master’s degrees, and 40 doctoral degrees. Our main campus is 1,136 acres, with additional acreage in University Farms, Touch of Nature Outdoor Education Center, and other facilities. The university is an essential part of the city of Carbondale and an important contributor to the culture of the entire region. While Carbondale includes many of the amenities of urban life, it retains its small-town flavor. Cost of living is considerably lower in the region than similar areas elsewhere, and many employees commute from nearby counties.


The Southern Illinois region is distinct from the rest of the state, boasting considerable natural beauty including the Shawnee National Forest, many state parks, national wildlife areas, and several lakes beloved for recreation. Local foods are readily available in the area, with a variety of eateries and a growing specialized food truck presence. The area is home to the Shawnee Hills Wine Trail, an official wine appellation designation. The wineries extend the cultural reach of the community, hosting live music and continual art exhibits. The campus itself is a microcosm of the area, with a lake and forest on campus, as well as traditional collegiate architecture, quad, and residential halls. Students enjoy outdoor study areas as well as specialized computer labs scattered across campus, including in the three million volume Morris Library. Job: Avian Field Technician - Appalachian Migratory Avian Monitoring 

Positions Open: 1

Agencies: West Virginia University

Location: Central and Southern West Virginia

Job Description: 1 month, April 27, 2027-May 27, 2027 . Full time, 5 days/week. Technician will assist one graduate student gather data on stopover sites of migratory bird species in early-succession forests through mist-netting, vegetation sampling, and deployment of autonomous recording units (ARUs). Through collaboration with the Cornell Lab eBird Program and the National Council for Air and Stream Improvement (NCASI), this project aims to learn more about how passerines (songbirds) are using regenerating timber harvests as stopover sites during migration. Filling in the knowledge gaps of how migratory birds use forest harvested forest landscapes is important to identify potential best forestry practices.

Expected duties include driving several hours each day, hiking long distances off trail in mountainous terrain while carrying field equipment to sites, and identifying avian species by sight. Other technician duties will include setting up and deploying ARUs for sites, setting up mist-nets, assisting in the banding/handling of live birds, and performing vegetation surveys. Interacting with private landowners and the public may be required. Field sites are remote and rugged with limited cell reception, although comfortable modern field housing will be provided. Field sites are close to the Monongahela National Forest as well as the New River Gorge National Park. 

Qualifications: Applicants should have a valid driver’s license, clean driving record, and must be able to perform field work full time. Applicants must be able to hike up to 8 miles a day in rugged terrain sometimes carrying up to 50 lbs. of gear in typical Appalachian spring/summer conditions. Must have experience identifying eastern songbirds by sight and sound, with emphasis on identification by sight. High preference will be given to applicants with previous mist-netting experience and experience backpacking. Also preferred is experience with collecting vegetative data (tree, shrub, and ephemeral ID) but training will be provided. Applicants working toward or holding B.S. degrees in wildlife biology, zoology, environmental science, or related fields are preferred. A strong work ethic, positive attitude, sense of curiosity, and attention to detail are essential.  

Send a cover letter, resume, and contact information for at least 3 references (must include email and phone number for each reference listed) by email to: [email removed] 

Salary: Stipend of $2,160/month or $540 a week. Shared housing and transportation to work is provided but technicians will need to have a vehicle for personal use. 

Application Deadline: January 1st, 2027

Start Date: April 27th, 2027

Contact: Ava Craven - [email removed]

Position Description
Cibola National Forest: Archeologist Project Organizer Individual Placement
Rocky Mountain Youth Corps (RMYC) is a nonprofit youth development organization serving New Mexico. We inspire young adults to make a positive difference in themselves and their communities. Through training and service, Corpsmembers discover their potential for healthy, productive lives.

Individual Placement positions work within RMYC partner agencies, and are intended to provide meaningful job experience for young professionals looking to build their careers in specific fields. This role will act as a lead to other individual placements.

POSITION OVERVIEW: The Archeological Project Organizer Individual Placement will support the Cibola National Forest – Heritage and Cultural Resource Department with project management, provide direction and training for field personnel, report production, GIS and data management, supervision of field crew, tracking budget, coordination with other Forest Service departments/staff, the State of New Mexico, members of the public and Forest Service volunteers.

Administrative responsibilities include collecting data, writing brief project reports, and communicating with Cibola NF and RMYC staff. 

This position is managed through RMYC and includes regular check-ins and life skills training. Other training opportunities will be provided through the host program or outside training tailored to the needs of the individual. Cross-training with other programs is also encouraged.

POSITION TYPE: Seasonal, full time

SCHEDULE: Full Time, 40 Hours per week, Monday-Friday 8am-5pm. Exact start and end times will be determined by program funding, program needs, and timing of applications received.

REPORTS TO: Cibola National Forest Staff daily and to RMYC Individual Placement Program Coordinator on a weekly basis.

LOCATION: Cibola National Forest/Magdalena Ranger District –Cultural Resources 203 First Street, Magdalena, NM 87825 

COMPENSATION: $29.90 (GS09 equivalency)

BENEFITS:

RMYC observes all National holidays and are considered approved paid days off.
BACKGROUND CHECK: A USDA background clearance must be completed before the selected candidate may report for service. The Forest Service will provide instructions for completion of the clearance after a candidate has been selected and will notify them when they have been cleared to start service. This process will determine the participant’s exact start date.

Participants will have access to government facilities and systems, and will be supplied with access to gov’t vehicles, equipment, and materials needed to work on the projects and activities as outlined above. Participants must adhere to all government regulations and policies for operating equipment, vehicles, security awareness, and safety.

Chosen candidates must complete a pre-employment National Service Criminal History Check and fingerprint scan with the following requirements:
You must be truthful in all statements regarding criminal history.
You cannot be registered or required to be registered on any state sex offender registry or the National Sex Offender Registry.
You cannot be convicted of murder.
ELIGIBILITY:

A chosen candidate must meet the following requirements:
Must be a citizen, national, or lawful permanent resident of the United States. State-level background checks will be conducted for non-residents of NM.
Insurable driving record and a valid driver’s license. Drivers must be over 21 or have had a license for at least 3 years.
Essential physical functions include the ability to sit, stand, walk, speak, hear, climb, balance, reach with hands & arms, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl on a frequent basis, and lift up to 50 pounds unassisted.
Field investigation involves considerable walking over rough, rocky surfaces, some bending and stretching. Average physical dexterity and ability are required. Fieldwork is performed in all weather conditions, occasionally in mountainous terrain. Sometimes primitive facilities must be used for extended periods.
Reasonable accommodations may be made for qualified individuals to perform the essential functions.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES: 

Able to manage the field and reporting process of a large cultural resource reconnaissance project.  
Supervise an archeology survey crew to direct field work, data collection and data processing. 
Assist staff with:
The development of immediate objectives, integration with resource activities, and establishment of priorities.
Budget and project plan of work for the unit’s archeological and cultural activities within the National Forest unit.
Design inventory strategies as part of the land use planning process based on Forest-wide priorities and needs.
Determining eligibility of historical properties for the National Register of Historic Places.
Providing heritage and cultural resource management orientation to Forest Service personnel on statutes, regulations and purpose of work to be performed.
Interpreting heritage and cultural resources to the public and professional contacts through presentations at visitor facilities, professional journals, etc.
Ensuring program data for documentation submission including contracts, National Register of Historic Places (NRHP) eligibility criteria, legal documents to fulfill programmatic requirements, and internal reports.
Organize, supervise, or directly perform inventory of areas to include preparation of maps, inventories, reports, and records related to the discovery, protection, inventory, salvage, and interpretation of heritage and cultural resource areas.
Review reports as part of project planning to evaluate the quality of the inventory, the completeness of the report, and the significance of heritage or cultural sites found; prepares determinations of effect for such projects identified during project inventories; assists staff with recommendation of mitigation procedures.
SECONDARY RESPONSIBILITIES: 

Participation and Expedition Behavior:

Work effectively as a member of a team despite potentially stressful and difficult conditions. This may require problem solving on an interpersonal or group level as well as a willingness to accept differences.
Contribute to a safe learning environment, no harassment of others for any reason.
Willingness and ability to complete all aspects of the program including conservation projects, education, training, and national service.
Effectively communicate ideas and concerns as they arise directly to supervisors, colleagues, and organization staff. 
Appropriately represent the U.S Forest Service to the public and partners at all times.
Flexibility, adaptability, and capacity to work in a fluid, changing work environment.

Safety and Judgment: 

Effectively communicate danger to others in the form of either a warning of danger others may be encountering or a notification of personal distress, injury or need for assistance. Must be able to do so at a distance of up to 50 meters and in conditions with limited visibility or loud background noise such as darkness or high winds.
Effectively perceive and understand significant and apparent hazards and follow direction by others so that you will be able to successfully execute techniques to manage hazards. These directions may be given before the hazard is encountered or may need to be given during the exposure to the hazard. Ability to respond appropriately to stress or crises.
Stay alert and focused for several hours at a time while traveling and working in varied weather conditions.
If taking prescription medications, participants must be able to maintain proper dosage by self- medicating without assistance from others.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

Bachelor’s Degree in Archeology/Anthropology or similar field.
At least 3-5 years of professional work experience in Archaeology.
Knowledge of:
Theories, principles, and techniques of archeology.
General knowledge of land management practices sufficient to prescribe a typical Heritage and Cultural Resource Management (CRM) Program in keeping with basic National Forest program requirements.
The broad patterns of the various cultures and archeology of the groups who inhabited the region in past periods, in order to adapt the CRM program to local conditions.
The various cultures and ethnic groups who inhabited the region in past periods to evaluate archeological findings and conduct surveys.
Limited knowledge of related disciplines such as timber management, hydrology, soils, plant pathology, wildlife habitat management, engineering, etc., sufficient to recognize how they relate to CRM issues and to recognize when specialized advice is necessary.
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:
Master’s degree in Archeology or related field
5-10 years of experience
Proficient in data collection and management of geospatial technology (ArcPro, FieldMaps, AGOL and Heritage NRM)

To apply, please submit an application to the Rocky Mountain Youth Corps application portal at https://youthcorps.org/apply-now including a resume and cover letter.
Rocky Mountain Youth Corps is available to all and we will not discriminate or refuse services to any staff or member because of perceived or actual race, color, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, political affiliation, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, marital or parental status, military service or pregnancy.
 RMYC is a drug free workplace. All positions are dependent upon funding availability.

Description
 Summary Description: The full-time Watershed Restoration Program Director provides strategic and operational leadership for Borderlands Restoration Network’s Watershed Restoration Program (WRP). The Director develops and oversees a portfolio of watershed restoration, ecological/watershed assessments, monitoring, and applied conservation projects across public and private lands throughout the U.S.-Mexico borderlands. 

The position requires a landscape-scale systems thinker who can integrate science, ecological processes, partnership development, and adaptive management to achieve long-term conservation impacts across diverse land ownerships and jurisdictions.

The Director is responsible for developing collaborative partnerships, securing funding, overseeing restoration planning and implementation, managing staff and budgets, and ensuring that science and monitoring inform restoration priorities and adaptive management. Success in this role requires balancing strategic leadership with practical implementation while recognizing that individual restoration projects contribute to broader watershed function, habitat connectivity, and long-term landscape resilience.
 
Supervises: Watershed Restoration Program Manager, Preserve Staff, and Restoration Specialist
 
Geographic Location: The Watershed Restoration Program is based in Patagonia, AZ. The WRP Director must be located in Patagonia or close enough to be physically in Patagonia during program execution.

Duties and Responsibilities:

1. Program Leadership & Strategic Planning 
Provide strategic leadership for the WRP and establish long-term program priorities aligned with BRN's mission and conservation strategy
Identify and prioritize watersheds, landscapes, partnerships, and restoration opportunities that advance long-term conservation goals
Evaluate new funding opportunities, partnerships, and projects by considering their strategic alignment, ecological benefit, organizational capacity, and financial feasibility
Participate in organization-wide strategic planning and conservation initiatives  
Foster innovation and continuous improvement through adaptive management and evidence-based decision-making

2. Restoration Project Development & Management 
Lead the planning, development, and implementation of watershed and ecological restoration projects from concept through completion
Oversee project schedules, budgets, contractors, staffing, deliverables, and compliance with grant, contract, and regulatory requirements 
Coordinate complex, multi-disciplinary restoration projects involving multiple funding sources, land ownerships, agencies, contractors, and partners
Ensure projects are implemented safely and efficiently 
Coordinate landowner/partner outreach and engagement to develop projects 
Ensure appropriate environmental compliance, permitting, and agency coordination

3. Monitoring, GIS, and Technical Leadership 
Develop and oversee ecological monitoring, GIS, and data management systems that evaluate restoration effectiveness and support adaptive management
Provide technical oversight and collaborate with the Restoration Specialist to analyze ecological and spatial data to inform restoration priorities and project evaluation
Translate science, monitoring results, and spatial analyses into practical restoration recommendations and management decisions

4. Grants, Partnerships, and Program Development 
Develop funding strategies and manage a diverse portfolio of grants, contracts, and cooperative agreements, including proposal development, budgeting, reporting, and compliance
Build and maintain collaborative partnerships with government agencies, nonprofit organizations, Tribal partners, private landowners, and funders
Represent BRN in collaborative working groups, technical committees, partner meetings, conferences, and other regional conservation initiatives  

5. Staff Leadership and Organizational Collaboration
Recruit, supervise, mentor, and develop Watershed Restoration Program staff
Establish work priorities, delegate responsibilities, and foster a collaborative, inclusive, and safety-oriented team culture 
Serve as a member of BRN’s leadership team and contribute to organizational planning, budgeting, and strategic initiatives
Collaborate across programs to align organizational priorities and maximize impact
Collaborate with BRN's Communications and Development Team to share program accomplishments through reports, presentations, newsletters, social media, outreach materials, the annual report, and other fundraising and public engagement efforts

The duties and responsibilities outlined above are representative of the position but are not intended to be all-inclusive. Responsibilities may evolve over time and additional duties may be assigned to support organizational priorities and program needs.

Requisite Education & Experience
Bachelor's degree in ecology, restoration, environmental science, watershed science, range management, natural resources, or a closely related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience
Minimum five years of progressively responsible experience in restoration, watershed management, conservation, or a related field, including at least two years of program or project management and staff supervision
Experience developing and implementing ecological restoration or nature-based solutions
Experience developing long-term conservation strategies or landscape-scale restoration initiatives
Experience managing grants, contracts, budgets, and multiple concurrent projects
Experience developing collaborative partnerships with agencies, nonprofit organizations, private landowners, or other stakeholders
Experience with grant writing, grant administration, technical reporting, and project compliance
Knowledge of watershed processes, ecological restoration principles, and regional conservation challenges
 
Required Skills, Knowledge, and Abilities
Strong leadership, organizational, and project management skills
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including technical writing and public speaking
Ability to manage competing priorities and make sound decisions in a dynamic environment
Ability to build collaborative relationships with diverse partners and stakeholders
Ability to analyze ecological and spatial information to support restoration planning and adaptive management
Proficiency with GIS, Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, and field data collection platforms
Ability to work independently while fostering collaboration across interdisciplinary teams
Commitment to safety, professionalism, integrity, and BRN's mission
Valid driver's license and ability to travel throughout the project area
Ability to obtain and maintain a valid passport 

Desired Skills, Knowledge, and Abilities
Master's degree in a related field
Knowledge of the ecology and conservation challenges of the Sky Island/U.S.–Mexico borderlands
Knowledge of and experience with environmental and cultural compliance (E.g. NEPA, ESA, SHPO, NHPA, etc) 
Experience with federal grants, contracts, or cooperative agreements
Experience with data analyses and statistical software like R 
Experience with ecological monitoring, remote sensing, drone mapping, or other emerging restoration technologies
Bilingual English/Spanish preferred

Physical Requirements: The physical demands described here are representative of those required to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Ability to work in both office and outdoor environments, including supervising and participating in restoration, monitoring, and assessment activities in remote locations and on uneven terrain
Ability to hike varying distances to project and monitoring sites while carrying light field equipment
Ability to sit or stand for extended periods and perform computer-based work, including frequent use of a computer, phone, and other electronic devices
Ability to communicate effectively in person, virtually, and by telephone with staff, partners, contractors, and the public
Ability to lift, carry, and move up to 30 pounds
Ability to travel regularly to field sites, partner meetings, conferences, and other work locations, including occasional overnight travel
Moderate noise levels are typical in both office and outdoor work environments

Email your resume and cover letter to Alexandria Hawkins at [email removed] by November 16th to be considered for this position. As this position has a start date as soon as possible, please indicate when you apply if you’re currently authorized to work in the United States.

FirstName_LastName_Resume

We encourage applicants to apply even if they only meet some of the qualifications listed. We value diverse experiences and are committed to providing training and support for the right candidate.

Description
The Bur Oak Land Trust AmeriCorps Program is essential to the management and restoration of Bur Oak Land Trust properties and other protected nature preserves on which the land trust serves in eastern Iowa. Field Crew Members will serve on a 4-person crew led by a Crew Leader to restore native habitat and remove invasive plant species. The crew will be trained in a variety of land management techniques including prescribed fire, chainsaw operation, herbicide application, and use of other tools to improve overall habitat quality on these sites.

Please submit both a resume and a cover letter to Sarah Lawinger for consideration. Applications without a cover letter will not be considered.

The position starts January 11, 2027 and ends December 17, 2027. The position is based out of Iowa City, IA with regular travel within Johnson, Muscatine, Poweshiek, and other surrounding counties. The service term for this position is 12 months, with a typical service schedule of 40 hours per week in the field, Monday through Friday (i.e. 8am-4pm). During summer months (May-August), member may be required to serve 40 hours Monday-Thursday (7am-5pm).

The Crew Member is responsible for serving a minimum of 1,700 hours, completing required service tasks, and serving until the December 2027 deadline to successfully complete their term.

Position responsibilities:
Complete an assigned task book before the end of the term. Task book skills will include:
Chainsaw operations skills including limbing, bucking, stumping, slash-cutting, and limited tree felling
Safe use of herbicide through cut-stump, basal bark, or foliar spray methods
Prescribed fire skills including ignition, suppression, and mop-up assignments
Use of a variety of other power and hand tools, including brushcutters, brush mowers, weed whips, leaf blowers, augers, and others
Cleaning and maintaining various equipment used to accomplish project tasks as assigned. Promptly alerting site supervisor of any mechanical issues or repairs.
Operate program vehicles including work trucks, trailers, UTVs, and ATVS safely at all times.
Plant and Tree Species Identification including, but not limited to: 5 woody invasive species, 7 less common woody invasive species, and 22 common tree species in winter form
External Training Courses (provided during the term): Iowa Commercial Pesticide Applicator Certifications (Iowa Core & Right-of-Way), Stop the Bleed, Prescribed Fire (NWCG): ICS 100, IS 700, S-130, S-190, L-180, and In-person Field Day.
AmeriCorps Disaster Response Team (optional, as opportunities arise):
Participate in A-DRT training(s) as necessary to ensure knowledge and ability to respond to disasters
Complete other training as necessary to support disaster deployments, including but not limited to Volunteer Reception Center (VRC), first aid, mental health first aid, and chainsaw training
Ensure availability for the term of the disaster deployments, generally 2-4 weeks. Make plans for pets, family members, other employment and responsibilities that need regular attention.

AmeriCorps required qualifications:
Must be a high school graduate or GED equivalent
Must be at least 17 years old or older at the start of service
Must pass a 3-part national service criminal history check
Must have a valid driver’s license or other government issued photo identification
Must hold one of the following citizenship statuses: US citizen, US national, or Lawful Permanent Resident

Preferred qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree or in pursuit of a bachelor's degree
Ability to lift 50 lbs
Ability to hike/walk up to 5 miles per day while carrying equipment
Manual labor experience

Benefits:
Position is eligible for an AmeriCorps Education Award upon successful completion of the program. Education Award amount: $7,395.00
Living allowance: $1,983.00 per month (pre-tax)
Health insurance
Student loan forbearance for eligible loans

All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply and will receive consideration for employment free from discrimination on the basis of race, creed, color, national origin, age, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, religion, associational preference, status as a qualified individual with a disability, or status as a protected veteran.

Please submit both a resume and a cover letter for consideration. Applications without a cover letter will not be considered.

GENERAL DESCRIPTION:
Under the direction of the DISTRICT 8 LEADER, this position is responsible for performing the professional planning and implementation of natural resource management, monitoring, and research duties associated with wildlife and habitat resources in Bastrop and Caldwell counties within the Post Oak Savannah ecological region of the Southern Blackland Prairie Wildlife District.  Provides technical assistance and public outreach programs to the general public, private landowners/land managers, sportsmen, and new constituencies. Develops comprehensive wildlife management plans for private landowners upon request.  Disseminates information to the general public through news releases, radio/TV interviews, program presentations, and other public outreach and educational opportunities.  Performs administrative duties and prepares technical reports, popular articles, and professional journal publications.  Responsible in assigned area for public relations and educational/extension efforts to involve private citizens and organizations in support of Texas Parks and Wildlife Department (TPWD) programs.  Identifies public hunting and non-consumptive use opportunities on public and private lands.  Performs additional duties as assigned.  Complies with all Agency, Division and Branch rules, regulations and procedures. 

NOTE:  Natural Resources Specialist (NRS) I salary will be commensurate with experience and/or completion of an advanced degree.  Current TPWD NRS I-III employees may apply for this position at their current classification title and at the established Wildlife Division salary rate. Career Ladder progression is available dependent upon business need. 

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

Education:
Graduation from an accredited college or university with a Bachelor's degree preferably in Wildlife Science, Wildlife Management, Wildlife Ecology, Range and Wildlife Management, or closely related field in Natural Resources Management.  Major coursework from Bachelor's or post-Bachelor's degree programs must include a minimum of 24 hours in Wildlife/Habitat Conservation, Wildlife/Natural Resources Management, Wildlife Biology, and/or Research Methods.

Experience:
NRS I: No experience required.
NRS II: Two years of relevant experience.
NRS III: Six years of relevant experience.

Must possess or be able to obtain, within 30 days of employment, a valid State driver's license.
Must possess or be able to obtain, within one year of employment, the National Wildfire Coordinating Group's (NWCG) Fire Fighter Type II (FFT II) certification. 

NOTE: Retention of position contingent upon obtaining and maintaining required license and certification.

Description
 Position Description: We are recruiting one MS student to conduct research which aims to assess strategies that can be used to accelerate the recovery of Masked Bobwhite, a critically endangered subspecies of the Northern Bobwhite. Previous efforts to recover Masked Bobwhite have focused on Buenos Aires National Wildlife Refuge, southern Arizona and have considered a variety of reintroduction techniques. Despite these efforts, a wild, self-sustaining population has not been achieved. To restore this iconic game bird this project will expand on previous efforts via an in situ captive study that aims to test approaches that lead to successful production and recruitment of Masked Bobwhite. It will also assess conditioning strategies (e.g., exposure to predator models) that promote survival and identify genetic markers linked to successful breeding and recruitment in this imperiled species. The project will combine field- and lab-based work to address these goals. The project is funded through the US Fish and Wildlife Service and students will be co-supervised by Dr. Jennifer Smith and Dr. Randy DeYoung. 

Key Responsibilities

·         Conduct fieldwork to meet project objectives, to include (1) monitoring breeding attempts and survival of Masked Bobwhite, and (2) assessing behavioral responses to conditioning approaches in experimental enclosures in the field, 
·         Conduct lab work to assess genetic markers linked to successful breeding and recruitment 
·         Manage field technicians during fieldwork 
·         Data management 
·         Apply statistical analysis used in assessments of e.g., habitat selection, migratory/dispersal decisions, space use 
·         Liaise and collaborate with private landowners and agency personnel 
·         Present research findings at conferences, in public forums, and via peer-reviewed journal articles 
 Qualifications Required: 

·         B.S. in ecology, wildlife biology, natural resources, or related discipline 
·         A minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) 
·         Demonstrated experience with statistical software (e.g., Program R) and GIS 
·         Excellent communication skills (written and verbal) 
·         Demonstrated research experience (data collection, analysis, writing) 
·         Ability to conduct fieldwork in hot conditions 

Preferred Qualifications 
·         Demonstrated involvement in trapping, handling, and banding birds 
·         Experience with lab work 
·         Experience with communicating with diverse stakeholders including members of government agencies, land managers, and members of the public 
 

Stipend/Salary:

(M.S.) $2,000/month stipend plus benefits (medical package available after completion of waiting period) and full tuition waiver (nonresident tuition waived-resident tuition fees apply but will be reimbursed to ensure a full tuition waiver) 
 Start Date: January 2026 is highly preferred, but we will also consider applicants for Summer 2026. 
 Application Deadline: We will begin reviewing applications on 11th November 2026 and will continue until a suitable candidate is selected. 

 To Apply: Submit an application packet as a single PDF including: (1) one-page letter of interest, (2) CV or resume, (3) unofficial undergraduate/graduate transcripts, and (4) contact information for two professional references to Dr. Jennifer Smith ([email removed]). 

For questions regarding this position:

Description
Pacific States Marine Fisheries Commission is recruiting candidates to fill the role of a Fishery Biologist 1 - Tagging Trailer Operator based in Red Bluff, California. This is a seasonal, benefits-eligible position with an anticipated start date of December 14th, 2026.
 
The Trailer Operator is responsible for operating and maintaining an automated fish-marking trailer that removes adipose fins and injects coded-wire tags (CWTs) into the snouts of juvenile salmon and steelhead. This is a highly technical position that requires strong troubleshooting skills, mechanical aptitude, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple systems simultaneously. Trailer Operators spend much of their time monitoring equipment performance, diagnosing problems, making adjustments, and maintaining the various components within the AutoFish trailer. These are complex systems with many processes occurring at once, making the position both challenging and rewarding. The Trailer Operator serves as the lead for an assigned shift and typically supervises one or two technicians, ensuring that fish are processed efficiently and accurately while maintaining equipment performance and quality-control standards. Additional information, photos, and videos of AutoFish systems can be found on the Northwest Marine Technology website.
 
This position offers valuable hands-on experience with both threatened and endangered salmonids while working at nine anadromous fish hatcheries throughout Northern California and collaborating with personnel from multiple agencies. For individuals who demonstrate the ability to learn, troubleshoot, and successfully operate these complex systems, opportunities for full-time, year-round employment may be available.
 
No Housing is provided.
 
Essential Functions:  
Lead and participate in survey crews that conduct fishery presence/absence research, recreational/commercial fishing surveys, anadromous fish escapement surveys (carcass, redd, trap/weir, snorkel, etc.), or tag detection and mark recovery surveys. Make standardized observations such as species identification, length, weight, behavior, growth, survival, reproductive condition, and/or signs of parasites, diseases or pathogens, fin clips or tags.
Lead and perform data entry for data from recovered tags, representative biological samples, telemetry devices, oceanographic data, fish tickets, commercial landing estimates, logbooks, scale cards, port sampling, onboard observers, etc. Error check the data, maintain and update database, analyze and organize data in the appropriate format (table, spreadsheet, memorandum, or report) necessary for transfer to individuals, agencies, and organizations. Modify software programs and perform data queries. Prepare summary reports to transfer data.
Lead crew or assist hatchery manager with maintenance of fish including feeding fish, cleaning tanks, establishing feeding schedules, assessing growth, and monitoring fish health. Collect samples of blood and tissues. Monitor and maintain facility systems, equipment, and water quality. Maintain records of data and perform routine analysis.
Knowledge Required by the Position:

Knowledge of fishery biology (including knowledge of particular species of fish).
Knowledge of fish husbandry.
Knowledge of aquatic habitats.
Knowledge of the scientific method.
Knowledge of personal computer applications such as word processing, spreadsheets, e-mail, publishing software, presentation software, database software, topographic software, bibliographic software, and statistical analysis packages.
Knowledge of technical writing protocols.
Knowledge of statistics and mathematics.
Knowledge of database management.
Knowledge of programming languages such as SQL .
Additional Mandatory Skills: 

elec. detection technology
lift 40-50 lbs.                                     
valid driver's license              
tow & maneuver trailers
fish species ID skills               
compile and collect neat and accurate data     
specific software skills (spreadsheet, word processing, database, GIS, statistical)
oral communication skills                  
written communication skills
construction, fabrication and installation skills  
repair & maintain equipment
Physical Demands:

Demands can range from sedentary, to moderate --where there is walking, climbing stairs and ladders, reaching, lifting, and bending, to rigorous.  In the latter case, the employee must be able to handle buckets of water or gear weighing up to 50 pounds.  Long daily periods of hiking, carrying equipment, swimming, and/or standing may be required.  Camping out for extended periods may be required. Some work requires the ability to maintain footing in fast-moving water.

 

Work Environment:

Some work is performed in an office setting with adequate lighting, heating and ventilation.  Some work may be performed in fish processing labs, fish holding areas, and/or in the field.  Employees may work on narrow, elevated walkways and platforms that are over or adjacent to water.  Field work involves exposure to all types of weather, slippery rocks or docks, trails, irregular terrain, insects, poison oak, rough or fast-moving water, or cold water temperatures. Work at high elevations or aboard boats may be required.


Qualifications
Minimum Qualification Requirements:
A range of education and experience may be presented.  At the lower end of the range, candidates must present successful completion of a full 4-year course of study in an accredited college or university leading to a bachelor's or higher degree that included a major in biological science with at least 6 semester hours in aquatic subjects and at least 12 semester hours in the animal sciences.

Description
Pacific States Marine Fisheries Commission is recruiting candidates to fill the role of a Fishery Biologist 3 to work closely with U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) researchers at the Klamath Falls Field Station (KFFS), serving as the project lead for sucker research on long-lived endangered Lost River and Shortnose suckers. This is a full-time, benefits-eligible position with an anticipated start date of January 4th, 2027.
 
We're looking for a curious, applied-minded fishery biologist to lead research using an exceptional long-term dataset, collaborate with biologists and data managers, and help answer questions that shape sucker recovery and water management in the Klamath Basin. This position has a leading role in advancing sucker research in the Klamath Basin, guiding one or more projects from study design and field data collection through analysis and publication. Working closely with field leads, partner agencies, and tribes, you'll help ensure management-relevant questions are answered, and that research provides actionable information for sucker recovery and water-management decisions.
 
The incumbent will have room to bring their own questions to the table, not just execute someone else's. This position also offers room for the successful candidate to help shape and pursue new research directions using the long-term dataset, including by developing and securing additional funding for questions of their own interest, as time and station priorities allow.
 
If you enjoy translating complex ecological data into answers managers can use, this position offers an opportunity to make a meaningful contribution to sucker recovery. We're looking for someone who gets energized by turning open biological questions into answers managers can actually use—someone curious enough to dig into two decades of individual-fish data and find what it can still tell us.
 
Please pay close attention to the required application materials and the closing disclaimer in the below sections.
 
Closing Disclaimer: PSMFC will not accept resumes or cover letters for any position once the job announcement has been removed from the Careers Page. PSMFC will begin reviewing submitted applications the week of November 16, 2026 and may begin
interviewing as soon as the week of November 23, 2026. PSMFC reserves the right to remove a job announcement at any time for any reason or close the position prior to the posted close date once a sufficient number of applicants have been received.
                         
Group Definition: Fishery Biologists use professional knowledge and competence in the science of fishery biology to perform work: (a) developing, conserving, propagating, managing, and administering fishery resources; (b) evaluating the impact of construction projects and other socioeconomic activities that present potential or actual adverse effects on fishery resources and their habitat; and (c) producing and managing aquatic resources in their natural habitat and/or within falities and systems that have been constructed for their benefit and public use.

Position/Project Specifics: The USGS Klamath Falls Field Station (KFFS) conducts research on rare and imperiled fish in the Klamath Basin, helping managers make informed decisions about resource use in a sensitive arid ecosystem.
 
For more than two decades, USGS KFFS researchers have been tracking individual Lost River and Shortnose suckers—two long-lived, endangered fish species—using passive integrated transponder (PIT) tags as part of a long-term capture-recapture effort. This exceptional dataset creates a rare opportunity to investigate patterns in wild fish populations over time.
 
The KFFS team has also been growing an acoustic telemetry program to go even further, tracking fish movement and survival in real time. The expanding program investigates seasonal movement, survival, and habitat use.
 
These data directly inform sucker recovery actions and water-management decisions in the Basin, connecting adult survival, recruitment, and lake conditions to management options.
 
The successful candidate will have opportunities to pursue research questions using these data, including determining methods for reducing parasite burdens, avoiding predation, relocating fish populations, and evaluating hatchery-driven supplementation efforts. Working with USGS Klamath Falls Field Station researchers, field leads, partner agencies, and tribes, the successful candidate will help shape research that addresses important biological questions and supports the recovery of these endangered species.
 
Essential Functions:  
PSMFC is seeking a Fishery Biologist 3 who is comfortable performing most of the below tasks. The ideal candidate will have experience leading or co-leading research projects from design through completion and publication and have 2+ years of work experience in addition to a PhD or Post-Doc.  
Perform complex tests and/or procedures that require using highly specialized methods or techniques 
Recognize and identify unusual and diverse entities, occurrences, or investigative outcomes relevant to the program area 
Modify or adapt established protocols and procedures in response to test or study findings Plan studies that require making significant departures from previous approaches 
Revise standard methods to improve or extend test and study systems
Recommend and approve studies. 
Participate in preparing briefing documents and communicating and coordinating with other staff 
Prepare and present technical studies and reports 
Contribute telemetry and capture-recapture expertise to fish passage and screening evaluations 
Assist in writing contract proposals and progress reports. Assist in developing detailed contract specifications, task statements, quality of work criteria, and other specifications. 
Monitor budget expenses for projects, control purchasing, and manage equipment inventories. 
Analyze and interpret complex biological and movement data, including Bayesian and state-space modeling 
Knowledge Required by the Position:

Knowledge of the theories, principles, and methods of Fishery Biology. 
Ability to define problems, perform background research, develop and execute a project plan, organize and evaluate results, and prepare reports of findings. 
Additional Mandatory Skills: 

Valid driver's license
Ability to apply quantitative and statistical methods to complex ecological datasets, including Bayesian modeling approaches for survival, movement, or population analysis. 
Ability to define problems, perform background research, develop and execute a project plan, organize and evaluate results, and prepare reports and publications of findings. 
Ability to design and adapt experimental protocols to address evolving management questions. 
Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, with scientific and management audiences. 
Ability to build and sustain productive working relationships with a broad range of partner agencies, tribes, and cooperators. 
Experience with acoustic telemetry study design, tag deployment, receiver array maintenance, and analysis of detection data. 
Experience with experimental design and statistical analysis of mark-recapture or movement datasets, including comfort working in a Bayesian modeling framework (e.g., JAGS, Stan, NIMBLE, or similar). 
Field experience with fish capture, tagging, and handling techniques. 
Familiarity with fish passage and screening issues as they relate to fish movement and survival (not required, but a plus). 
Some background in salmonid research is a plus, though not required. 
Experience with PIT-tag or other mark-recapture technologies. 
Experience coding in R or Python for data management and analysis; ability to effectively use AI tools to support coding, analysis, or writing workflows is a plus. 
Demonstrated experience securing funding for research projects, including writing competitive grant proposals, developing project budgets, and identifying and pursuing federal, state, and private funding opportunities. 
Additional Desirable Skills:

Knowledge of budget development and project management practices. 
Knowledge of acoustic telemetry and/or PIT-tag technologies and their application to long-term monitoring programs. 
Ability to code in R or Python for data management and analysis, or similar coding languages. 
Physical Demands:

The work is sedentary with moderate walking between workstations and carrying folders, reports, and similar light loads.

 

Work Environment:

The work is performed in an office setting with adequate lighting, heating and ventilation. There are the normal risks of an office environment. 

 

PSMFC is an EEO/AAP employer. We maintain a drug free workplace.


Qualifications
 Minimum Qualification Requirements:
Candidates must present successful completion of a full 4-year course of study in an accredited college or university leading to a bachelor’s or higher degree that included a major in biological science with at least 6 semester hours in aquatic subjects and at least 12 semester hours in the animal sciences. In addition, candidates must also present 1 year of Specialized Experience** AND a Ph.D. or equivalent doctorate degree in fields directly related to the position being filled. An equivalent combination of experience and education is also qualifying, such as a master's degree in fisheries biology, ecology, or a closely related field, with additional years of  Specialized Experience,* 

**Specialized Experience is experience that equips the applicant with the knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform successfully the duties of the position and is typically in or related to the work of the position being filled. To be creditable, specialized experience must have been equivalent to at least the next lower level in the normal line of progression for the position being filled.

To work with USGS Data Systems, the Candidate must also meet the below minimum requirements: 
Federal System Access: Must meet federal eligibility requirements to access and utilize federal data systems.

Job Description: 

This position is located at the DelAtlantic Conservation District (DACD) Office. DelAtlantic Conservation District works in cooperation with the New Jersey State Agriculture Development Committee (SADC) to provide technical and financial assistance to preserved farm landowners to encourage the implementation of conservation practices designed to address natural resource issues.
